VII. NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR CONTROL OF BLINDNESS
7.1 The National Programme for Control of Blindness was launched in the year 1976 as a 100%
Centrally-Sponsored scheme with the goal to reduce the prevalence of blindness from 1.4% to
0.3%. As per Survey in 2001-02, prevalence of blindness is estimated to be 1.1%. Target for the
Tenth Plan to reduce prevalence of blindness to 0.8% by 2007 could not be reached but the
prevalence rate of blindness has reduced to 1%.
7.2 Plan allocation of Rs.140.00 crores provided in 2007-08 was enhanced to Rs.171.87 crore
at RE stage. Enhanced allocation of Rs.250.00 crores has been made for 2008-09. The Committee
observes that upto 29.2.2008, utilization of Rs.120.62 crore has been reported.
7.3 The Committee has been given to understand that following new initiatives are proposed to
be taken with the enhanced provision of Rs.250.00 crores in 2008-09:—
1. Construction of dedicated Eye Wings and Eye OTs in District Hospitals in North-Eastern
States, Bihar, Jharkhand, J and K, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and few other States
where dedicated Operation Theaters are not available as per demand.
2. Appointment of the following Manpower:

64
1. Ophthalmic Surgeons In New Districts in District Hospitals.
2. Ophthalmic Assistants
3. Ophthalmic Assistants In PHCs/Vision Centers, where they are not available.
4. Eye Donation Counsellors In Eye Banks under Government Sector and NGO Sector
3. Grant-in-aid to NGOs for management of other Eye diseases other than Cataract like
Diabetic Retinopathy, Glaucoma Management, Laser Techniques, Corneal
Transplantation, Vitreo-retinal Surgery, Treatment of childhood blindness etc. of Rs.750
per case for Cataract/IOL Implantation Surgery and Rs.I000 per case of other major
Eye Diseases as described above.
4. Development of Mobile Ophthalmic Units in NE States, Hilly States & difficult terrains
for diagnosis and medical management of eye diseases.
5. Involvement of Private Practitioners in Sub District, Blocks and Village Level.
6. Maintenance of Ophthalmic Equipments supplied to Regional Institutes of
Ophthalmology, Medical Colleges, District/Sub-District Hospitals, PHCs/Vision Centres.
The Committee endorses the new initiatives that the Department has proposed for initiating
during the Eleventh Five Year Plan under NPCB. The Committee feels that such measures with
focused attention on NE States and also in the States of Bihar, Jharkhand, J and K, Himachal
Pradesh and Uttarakhand would surely go a long way in paving way for accessible eye-care for
the people in those regions where presently there is dearth of proper eye-care facilities.
7.4 The Committee is, however, surprised to find that implementation of new initiatives
depends on the approval of EFC Memo by the Ministry of Finance and CCEA. Till then, the
funds allocated for 2008-09 will continue to be utilized as per the existing scheme approved
for the Tenth Plan. The Committee is not happy with this state-of-affairs. Second year of
Eleventh Plan has already started and by the time approval of the competent authority is
finally received, the year 2008-09 would be nearing its end. The Committee would like to
point out that some of the new initiatives like construction of dedicated Eye Wings/Eye OTs
in District Hospitals, appointment of manpower, development of mobile Ophthalmic Units in
NE States will have to undergo a number of procedural formalities before their actually
taking off. The Committee accordingly recommends that concerted efforts need to be made
for getting the formal approval at the earliest. The Committee would appreciate if
simultaneously preparatory activities are also started.
7.5 As per the existing scheme under the Programme, the NGOs perform cataract operations
directly under the supervision of Respective District Blindness Control Societies, which function
under the State Blindness Control Society at the State level. To a query regarding the monitoring of
the working of 881 NGOs hospitals with eye-care facilities spread over in different parts of the
country, the Committee has been informed that working of NGO hospitals with eye care facilities
participating under NPCB are being monitored by the respective District Blindness Control Societies
directly. However, during State level meetings organized under the programme, NGOs’ hospitals are
also invited and the work done by them is reviewed. In addition, general guidelines for pre-operative,
operative and post-operative precautions for eye surgery have been circulated to all States from time
to time and last time these were circulated in the year 2007-08 to avoid eye mishaps.
The Committee has been taking note of instances of malfunctioning of Eye Camps
reported in the Media in the different States. The Committee feels that monitoring of Eye
Camps is being exclusively done by the District Blindness Control Societies. Department’s

65
role starts as and when reports regarding malfunctioning of Eye Camps held in States are
brought to the notice of the Ministry. Corrective measures are accordingly taken by the
Ministry. The Committee, however, feels that the Department needs to be more pro-active
in such cases. One corrective measure which can be initiated by the Department without
any special efforts involved is to review the performance of such Eye Camps in the State
level meetings, with required follow-up action taken on the reported incidents of
malfunctioning of Eye Camps. The Committee is also of the view that follow-up treatment
after Eye Camps should be made mandatory and strictly enforced. District hospital
authorities also need to be involved in the conducting of such Eye Camps by introduction
of compulsory, pre-checks in Eye Camps before start of Eye surgery and other treatment.
The Committee would like to add here that the Department should also devise some method
of surprise inspection of such eye camps organized by the NGOs to facilitate cataract
operations. This, the Committee feels, would ensure stricter compliance by all the concerned
entities and help reduce eyes mishaps. The Committee notes that the process for
independent evaluation of NPCB including evaluation of work being done by NGOs has been
initiated. The Committee would appreciate if this exercise is expedited so that corrective
measures are taken at the earliest.
7.6 It had come to the notice of the Committee that collection rate of eyes donated remained
discouraging inspite of IEC activities. The Committee notes that during 2004-05, number of eyes
donated was 23,553, followed by 28,007 in 2005-06 and 30,034 in 2006-07, with States like Goa,
H.P., Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, showing nil
performance. The Department has informed that at present, as per information available, about
30,000 donated eyes are collected annually in the country against the requirement of at least 80,000
to 1,00,000 of corneas per year for transplantation purpose.
7.7 The Department has informed that in order to encourage eye donation among masses, IEC
activities are being intensified under the programme. The major focus towards this direction is
organization of National Eye Donation Fortnight from 25th August to 7th September every year.
During the fortnight, intensified publicity through all available media is given to step up eye
donation campaign and persuade people to donate eyes after death. The focus of the fortnight has
been shifted from “Pledging of Eyes” to “Actual Collection of Eyes” by launching “Hospital
Retrievable Programme” in major hospitals with various specialties, teaching hospitals attached to
medical colleges and large multi-specialty hospitals in Government and Non-Government Sector,
Army, Railways, ESI and Industrial Establishments of the Country. In addition to this, the message
for eye donation is being propagated through various print and electronic media.
The Committee is not convinced that the IEC activities are being carried out as
intensely as is stated by the Department. The Committee has been given to understand that
out of the total allocated budget under National Programme for Control of Blindness,
around 7% has been spent on IEC, which according to the Committee, is quite a sizable
amount. The Committee strongly feels that public awareness about the noble cause of eye
donation for blind persons continues to be very low. The Committee is of the view that a
review of IEC activities on this aspect need to be made in consultation with all the stake
holders, specially reputed Eye Hospitals/NGOs doing commendable work in this area and
also both Government and private ad agencies. The Committee would also like to emphasise
that the functioning of Eye Banks in the country requires to be reviewed in view of reported
lack of logistic support for timely collection of eyes by the Eye Banks. Steps also need to
be taken for increasing the number of Eye Banks in the country.
7.8 The Department has informed the Committee that the Rapid Survey on Avoidable Blindness
was conducted in randomly selected 16 districts of 15 States (including two Districts from Uttar

66
Pradesh). The study was carried out by the Department of Community Ophthalmology, Dr.R.P.
Centre for Ophthalmic Sciences, AIIMS, New Delhi. The three disturbing findings of said survey
are as follows:—
• Performance of States of Orissa (Ganjam district) and West Bengal (Malda district)
needs to be augmented so that the gains of the technological revolution in eye care can
be effectively harnessed across the country.
• Cataract remains the single largest cause of blindness, low vision and one eye blindness
in India if the data of the 16 districts are pooled together.
• The prevalence of blindness in general population is 1%.
7.9 The Committee’s attention has also been drawn to the findings of a survey on Rapid
Assessment of TRACHOMA cases done in the district in States of Haryana, Gujarat, U.P.,
Uttarakhand, Punjab and Rajashtan. Findings of this survey were that against the popular perception
of there being no transmission of trachoma cases in India, all districts showed active cases.
The Committee notes with disappointment that the target to bring prevalence of
blindness to 0.8% by 2007 has not been reached. The Department has informed that as per
the report of Rapid Survey on Avoidable Blindness (2007), the prevalence of blindness has
come down to 1% and that Cataract remains the single largest cause of blindness, low
vision and one eye blindness in India. The Committee also infers from the above study that
the prevalence of blindness due to Trachoma also continues to be there. It is a well known
fact that blindness is a bane of nature. The Committee believes that most of the people in
smaller towns and rural areas are not aware of the symptoms of the above ailments, and
the methods to manage eye care, their eye-care service seeking behaviour pattern do not
change. The Committee exhorts the Department to take all possible necessary steps to
devise IEC activities in local media and television channels so that awareness among the
people is increased. The Committee believes a lot of cases of blindness can be checked by
such a measure and would in the long run help to achieve the targeted goals under the
programme.

ROUTINE IMMUNISATION PROGRAMME
9.14 The Committee has been observing the trend of under-utilization of allocated funds
under this programme. For 2006-07 against an allocation of Rs.345.00 crore, utilization of only
Rs.228.83 crores could be made. In 2007-08, position was very unsatisfactory. Allocation of
Rs.317.00 crore had to be reduced to Rs.260.00 crore and expenditure reported upto 29.02.08 is
only Rs.171.88 crores. Delayed procurement procedure has been cited as the main factor for
reduced allocation and utilization thereof during 2007-08. The Committee observes that an enhanced
allocation of Rs.615.00 crores has been kept for 2008-09 as it is proposed to use Hepatitis-B
Combo-vaccine (DPT+Hepatitis) from 2008-09.
9.15 The Committee has been observing that State specific problems specially in the low
performing States continue to persist. Shortage of Health Workers, lack of awareness and
laxity in monitoring and supervision of the programme are some of the problems being
noticed in such States. Reported coverage of different vaccines under the Routine
Immunization Programme confirms the Committee’s apprehensions that in some of the
States like Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Manipur, position is very unsatisfactory.
The Committee would like to point out that the steps taken for strengthening the Routine
Immunization Programme like recruitment of health workers, regular reviews at all levels
and catch up rounds in poor performing States do not seem to have yielded the desired
results. The Committee can only say that catch-up rounds in poor performance States with
the districts identified before hand is the most important step for effective reduction in the
number of un-immunized and partially immunized children. Entire focus of the
implementing agencies should be on this alone.
9.16 The Committee understands that the three pioneer institutes namely Central
Research Institute (CRI), Kasauli in Himachal Pradesh, Pasteur Institute of India (PTI),
Koonoor, Tamil Nadu and the BCG Vaccine Laboratory (BCGVL) in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
have been directed to stop vaccine production. The Committee strongly feels that these
vaccine production units should not be converted to only testing laboratories. The
Committee accordingly, recommends that the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare should
withdraw the order without delay.

OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
PART-A HEALTH SECTOR
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee observes that Oversight Committee has been granted only
Rs.100.00 crores against last year’s approved outlay of Rs. 600 crores, which, however, could
not be utilized. In the light of the recent Supreme Court’s judgment and the Government’s
propensity towards implementing it from this year itself, the Committee opines that the
funds would not be sufficient. Similarly against proposal of Rs.453.00 crores, only
Rs. 329.00 have been provided to CGHS; against projected requirement of Rs.87.88 crores,
Safdarjung Hospital has received Rs.50.00 crore; Dr. RML Hospital has been allocated
Rs.59.20 crore against projected Plan requirement of Rs.72.11 crore and Rs.68.95 crore
against Non-Plan requirement of Rs.71.88 crore; AIIMS has been granted Rs.452.00 crore
in Grant-in-Aids against projected requirement of Rs.753.00 crore and against the projected
total requirement of JIPMER for Rs. 150.80 crore, it has received only Rs.98.00 crore. The
Committee observes that under provisioning in many of the institutes is likely to adversely.
affect the completion of construction and developmental activities undertaken by them and
in the process the institutions. (Para 2.3)
The Committee notes that the overall allocation for the health sector (outside
NRHM) has been on the higher side. Still, the Committee is constrained to note that the
Department has failed to project its budgetary requirements in an effective way for the
simple reason that the utilization of funds during the Tenth Plan is far from satisfactory
which is evident from the fact that the sanctioned BE for 2005-06 and 2006-07 was
Rs.4253.84 crore and Rs.3564.95 crore, respectively, which was reduced to Rs.4096.25 crore
and Rs.3433.02 crore, respectively at the RE stage. The actual expenditure figures of
Rs.2907.96 crore and Rs.3377.34 crore were even less than the budgeted allocations at the
RE stage. The Committee notes that this trend has continued during 2007-08 also. This goes
to illustrate that the Department’s record in utilization of the allocated funds is below par.
The Committee would, therefore, recommend the Department to first ensure optimum and
judicious utilization of the funds allocated instead of highlighting the reduced budgetary
allocation. The Committee also recommends to the Department to take substantive steps so
that the stumbling blocks in the utilization of sanctioned funds for 2008-09 for a crucial
sector like health, are removed. (Para 2.4)
The Committee would like to point out that expenditure reported upto
29th February, 2008 was only Rs.1608.59 crores and within a span of three weeks it has
reached to Rs.2121.24 crores. This clearly indicates that major utilization is taking place in
the last quarter of the year. (Para 2.6)
The Committee observes that in spite of its raising concerns over this trend of under-
utilization of funds year after year, there does not seem to be any noticeable improvement
in this regard. Time and again the Committee has been advocating for higher allocation of
funds for this sector and this time the Committee is happy to note that the approved outlay
has seen a 32% hike over the last year’s Revised Estimate. The Committee reiterates its
concern and recommends to the Department to play a more pro-active role in identifying
72

73
the problems afflicting the utilization of funds in the Health Sector and initiate remedial
measures from the very beginning of the current financial year so that the old story of
revising estimates downwards and subsequent underutilization does not recur. (Para 2.7)
The Committee views with serious concern the under-utilization of funds on account
of slow pace of expenditure on implementation of schemes like Pradhan Mantri Swasthya
Suraksha Y ojna (PMSSY), Cancer, Mental Health, Capacity Building Project for Food and
Drugs, non implementation of the recommendations of the Over-sight Committee, New
Initiatives, and also non-finalizations of proposals relating to procurement of various
equipments, non filling up of vacant posts, non receipt of proposals from State Government/
Implementing Agencies etc. The Committee recommends the Department to keep the
activities of these schemes/institutions under constant monitoring so as to arrest this trend
of under utilization. (Para 2.8)
The pendency level of Utilization Certificates has been engaging the attention of the
Committee for the last few years. According to latest figures as on 1st March, 2008, there
were as many as 1318 Utilization Certificates in respect of Health Sector amounting to
Rs.677.61 crores for the grants released upto 2005-06. On a specific query regarding any
plans of the Department to reach a justifiable level of pendency, the Committee is given
to understand that a communication was sent by the Chief Controller of Accounts (CCA)
to all the States through Resident Commissioners on this issue giving full details of pending
UCs in respect of the Department of Health and Family Welfare. The Committee is
dismayed to note that in the name of efforts, only a letter has been issued. The Committee
feels that spirited efforts, which are apparently lacking, need to be made on priority basis
to clear the UCs which are pending for the last three decades or so. The Committee also
recommends to the Department to take up the case with concerned State Governments at
the highest level so as to assess whether the funds have been utilized properly or not.
(Para 2.9)
The Committee welcomes the proposal of the Department to introduce a provision in
the Sanction itself regarding audit of all centrally sponsored programmes, PSUs under the
Department and autonomous bodies which are receiving Grant-in-Aid. The Committee
recommends to the Department to expedite the same and intimate the progress made in
this regard. (Para 2.11)
Besides the names of Bodies/Programmes which would be covered during 2008-09, the
Committee would like to be informed about the centrally sponsored health programmes,
PSUs and autonomous bodies which were audited during 2007-08 along with the adverse
audit findings and the action taken by the Department thereon. (Para 2.12)
The Committee’s attention has been drawn by high level of pendency of Audit paras
contained in CAG Report and Internal Audit on matters relating to the Department. The
Committee is surprised to note that there are 62 pending Audit paras dating back from
CAG Report No.2 of 1998 to the latest CAG Report No. 20 of 2007 on the Performance Audit
of procurement of medicines and medical equipment. The Committee fails to understand the
reasons for such high level of pendency. The very fact that such a large number of Audit
paras remain to be reconciled indicates that internal financial management of the Ministry
is weak. The Committee would like to be apprised about the corrective measures taken in
the light of the pending Audit paras. (Para 2.13)
III. CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HEALTH SCHEME (CGHS)
The Committee notes that Plan allocation for 2008-09 is at an enhanced level when

74
compared with provision of Rs.40.00 crore made for 2007-08. As per the Outcome Budget
(2008-09), against a Plan allocation of Rs.40.00 crore for 2007-08 under CGHS, expenditure
reported upto 29.02.2008 is only Rs.19.08 crore. The Committee is, however, surprised to
note that in response to a specific query made by it, utilization of Rs.32.16 crore was
reported upto February, 2008. The Committee is unhappy with the conflicting figures of
utilization of plan funds. Either the information published in the Outcome Budget is
incorrect or inaccurate status report has been furnished to the Committee, that too on a
specific query made by it. Both the positions compel the Committee to conclude that there
is a need for better management at the Department level. The Committee apprehends that
chances are there that major utilization under CGHS has taken place during the last
quarter of the year. If it is true, this indicates improper handling of the funds. The trend
of utilization of major chunk of funds during the last quarter is not a healthy sign. The
Committee would like to be apprised about utilization of Plan and Non-Plan funds (quarter-
wise) during 2007-08. In the light of last year’s experience of utilization of funds, the
Committee recommends that concerted efforts need to be made for optimum and judicious
utilization of enhanced allocation made for 2008-09. (Para 3.2)
The Committee, therefore, recommends that allocation of funds under Non-Plan be
enhanced adequately so that the services available to the CGHS beneficiaries are not
affected. (Para 3.3)
The computerization of CGHS dispensaries and offices in Delhi was taken up at an
expenditure of Rs.8.74 crores. The Committee was informed that as on 26.3.08, 83
dispensaries in Delhi have been fully computerized and the process of computerization of
remaining 4 dispensaries was under way. The Committee would like to point out that
computerization process of CGHS dispensaries in Delhi could not be completed as scheduled.
Originally targeted to be completed by 2006-07, revised date of 17th  August, 2007 could also
not be adhered to. By the end of financial year, 2007-08, 4 dispensaries in Delhi still
remained to be computerized. Computerization of CGHS dispensaries located in Mumbai,
Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad, Nagpur and Pune to be taken up in 2007-08 as scheduled is
yet to start. The Committee can imagine the status of third phase slated to be completed
in 2008-09. The Committee, keeping in view the past experience in respect of Delhi
dispensaries, can only emphasize that all steps need to be taken to complete the
computerization of dispensaries outside Delhi at the earliest. Corrective measures based on
the problem areas noticed in the computerization of dispensaries in Delhi need to be taken.
(Para 3.4)
The Committee would like to point out that situation is some what different.
Problems are being faced both by the CGHS functionaries and beneficiaries. Technicians,
Junior staff manning counters in dispensaries and attending doctors need to be fully
trained. Practical problems like internet and electricity failure have to be tackled by having
an alternative arrangement. These initial teething problems should not be allowed to be
prolonged. At present, beneficiaries which include senior citizens also are being made to
wait for hours at the dispensaries. Their ordeal starts right from the registration counter
and continues upto delivery of medicines. The Committee would appreciate if all the
measures including training, smooth running of computers with full connectivity, backup for
power failure are taken at the earliest and also closely monitored. (Para 3.5)
The Committee has been emphasizing for long for introduction of two shift system
in CGHS. The Committee does not appreciate the contention of the Ministry that a large
number of private hospitals and diagnostic centres have been empanelled under the CGHS
and in case of emergency, beneficiaries can go there for treatment and claim re-

75
imbursement later. The Committee would like to draw the attention of the Ministry once
again to the fact that idea behind having two shifts in CGGS dispensaries is the
inconvenience being faced by the CGHS beneficiaries, majority of them office goers in going
to the dispensaries in the morning hours. The Committee is disturbed by the element of
helplessness shown by the Ministry in their candid admission of staff side vehemently
opposing the move. In this era where the service providers like banks etc. are opting for
flexible timings to give their customers maximum possible services, at least the Ministry
could have come forward with a positive and proactive approach. The Committee would
reiterate its recommendation made last year for starting two shifts in a few dispensaries as
a test case. One must not forget that CGHS is a service oriented scheme, supposedly
providing health care mainly to our serving employees and pensioners. It is the
responsibility of the Ministry to make the CGHS employees understand and not to be
pressurized by them. (Para 3.6)
The Committee recommends that construction of dispensary in Dwarka where land
is already available should start at the earliest. All procedural formalities should be
expedited and completion of project strictly monitored. (Para 3.7)
The Committee is surprised to note that even after two years, suitable
accommodation for housing the dispensary in Sector 82, Noida and Gurgaon could not be
managed. Secretary (Health) Government of Haryana is now being requested to allot a
building for CGHS Dispensary in Gurgaon. Proposal for housing the CGHS Dispensary in
Community Centre, Sector 82, Noida on rent-basis is under consideration. The Committee
strongly feels that the Ministry should pursue the two proposals in hand so that large
number of CGHS beneficiaries residing in these two areas do not continue to remain
deprived of health care any more. (Para 3.8)
The Committee recommends to the Department to take the issue on priority with the
Ministry of Finance to complete all the procedural formalities, so that necessary posts are
created and subsequently filled up. The Committee would also like to be apprised about the
cadre strength created as a result of implementation of SIU report and the efforts taken
so far to fill up the vacant posts. (Para 3.9)
The Committee understands that third party administrators for processing of claims
and medical audit are also proposed to be introduced. The Committee has been given to
understand that as recommended by SIU, Department of Expenditure, vacancies arising in
Group ‘D’ posts are to be progressively outsourced. (Para 3.10)
The Committee views with serious concern the growing number of vacancies in
different categories of posts in CGHS dispensaries. The Committee understands that all
surplus posts identified in cities outside Delhi have been abolished. It has also been
informed that the staff strength in the dispensaries is decided as per the workload. The
very fact that at the present juncture, no CGHS city can be stated to have full complement
of the staff strength as per the SIU norms establishes that the existing dispensaries are not
functioning as envisaged. The Committee also strongly feels that outsourcing /hiring of staff
on contract-basis on a big scale is a remedy worse then the disease. The concept of public
private partnership cannot be applied across the board specially in a set-up meant for
providing health care. The Committee would like to have a status note on the sanctioned
posts and vacancies category-wise and region-wise in CGHS dispensaries. (Para 3.11)
The Committee recommends that all out efforts be made for reduction in the
consultation fees to 2 per cent for procurement of drugs/medicines for CGHS as assured by
the Ministry and the Committee be informed accordingly. (Para 3.12)

76
The Committee is happy to note that these adhoc arrangements would continue until
further orders. The Committee would, however, like to emphasize that empanelment of
these hospitals on permanent basis should be made, specially in view of cancer patients
undergoing prolonged and costly treatment. The Ministry has to playa proactive role in such
matters. (Para 3.13)
The Committee notes that under the revised exercise, rates in respect of Bangalore,
Chennai, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur and Pune have been
issued. The Committee hopes that rates for the remaining cities would be issued at the
earliest. The Committee would like to be apprised about the level of difference in the rates
for major hospitals/diagnostic centres in the metro cities. (Para 3.14)
IV. SAFDARJUNG HOSPITAL AND V ARDHMAN MAHAVEER MEDICAL COLLEGE,
NEW DELHI
The Committee, however, notes that upto 29.02.2008 expenditure of only
Rs.53.77 crore could be reported. (Para 4.2)
The Committee apprehends that the present allocation of funds to the Hospital might
adversely affect its services and in the process, the large number of patients. While
cautioning the Hospital to utilize its allocated funds judiciously and optimally, the
Committee recommends that it should be granted adequate funds to meet its functional
requirements. (Para 4.3)
The Committee observes that procedures and rules are made to streamline,
strengthen and facilitate a process and not create hurdles and bottlenecks. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that effective coordination between the Department and the Hospital
authorities is required in this regard. If required, suitable steps for improvement in
the procedural aspect may be initiated so as to provide better health care delivery system.
(Para 4.4)
The Committee is happy to note that scheme of redevelopments of hospitals
including redevelopment of Safdarjung Hospital with the proposal to increase its bed
strength from 1531 to 3000 has finally been included in the approved schemes for the
Eleventh Plan. HSCC has submitted a final report on ‘Redevelopment Plan of Safdarjung
Hospital’ to the Department for consideration. The Department has started work for
engaging consultants for preparation of DPR for the detailed redevelopment plan. The
Committee would like to point out that ‘in principle’ approval by the Planning Commission
has already taken considerable time. The Committee therefore, urges the Department to
make wholehearted efforts to expedite the procedural formalities at the earliest. The
redevelopment plan is required to be started without any further delay, keeping in view the
ever-increasing patient load on the Safdarjung Hospital. The Committee recommends
that scarcity of funds and lack of coordination should not come in the way of its
timely completion and the Department should make every conceivable effort in this regard.
(Para 4.5)
The Committee expresses its serious concern on the slow progress made with regard
to setting up of Renal Transplantation Unit. Status of the project for IVF unit is more
discouraging as ‘in principle’ approval is yet to come. The Committee can only emphasize
that the Renal Transplantation Unit should be made functional by the year end by closely
monitoring the progress of the same. Procedural formalities with regard to IVF unit also
need to be completed at the earliest. (Para 4.7)

77
The Committee’s attention has been drawn by a large number of vacancies in
different categories of posts in Safdarjung Hospital. Out of the total sanctioned staff
strength of 4781, there were 1054 vacant posts in different categories as on July, 2007. The
Committee has been given to understand that workload of the Hospital has progressively
increased manifold in the past few years. The doctor patient ratio has inversely grown,
there is an acute need of more doctors per patient and related infrastructure including
sub-staff. In such a scenario, with the redevelopment project of Safdarjung Hospital likely
to take off at the earliest, additional staff strength of all the categories would be required.
The Committee, accordingly, recommends that the Department in co-ordination with
hospital authorities should chalk out an action-plan for acquiring the required manpower.
(Para 4.8)

The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of an assurance that each Central
Institute will have a separate monitoring Committee, given by the Secretary, H&FW before
the Committee last year, no action seems to have been taken. The Committee, therefore,
reiterates that a proper monitoring mechanism needs to be put in place so as to arrest this
trend of sub-optimal utilization of the funds. (Para 5.2)
The Committee has been observing that a number of projects-big and small
envisaged for strengthening and augmenting the existing services in the premier hospital
continue to remain in the implementation status with very little progress being made. The
Committee has been constrained to point out that the year 2007-08 was also no exception.
Funds allocated remained under-utilised with the following three major projects running
behind schedule:—
• Strengthening of Accidents and Emergency Department and setting up of Trauma
Care Centre.
• Setting up of PGIMER at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.
• Upgradation of School of Nursing into College of Nursing.
All these projects were to be completed in 2007-08 only. The Committee notes that
academic session for PG Courses in Medicine, Paediatrics and Anesthesia is to begin in
2008-09. While welcoming the starting of PGIMER at Dr. RML Hospital, the Committee
would appreciate if the PGI becomes fully operational running all the courses with the
required infrastructure and regular staff in place. The Committee apprehends that there is
little chance of Trauma Care Centre becoming operational in 2008-09 with appointment of
178 additional staff yet to be made and process of purchase of equipment and consumable

the upgradation of School of Nursing into College of Nursing. The target remains the same

The Committee was informed that the allocated funds would not be sufficient for
maintaining the infrastructure and patient care services of the Institute. The Committee
feels that the decrease in non-plan from Rs.310.00 crores in 2007-08 to Rs.290.00 crores is
surely going to affect the patient care services offered by the Institute. The Committee
apprehends return of the ‘user charges regime’ in AIIMS because consumables are the only
negotiable component of the non-plan budget as salary and bills have to be paid any way.

78

Plan period does not seem to have any visible impact. Plan provision of Rs.200.00 crore for
2007-08 not only remains at the same level as in the previous plan period but has also been
brought down to Rs.160.00 crore at the RE stage with actual expenditure reported up to
29.02.2008 being only Rs.113.33 crore. The Committee is not able to comprehend the
reasons for under-utilization of funds duly allocated for specific purposes. Failure on the
part of a premier institute like AIIMS to utilize the funds as targeted indicates that
problem areas continue to persist both in the co-ordination between the administrative
Ministry and the Institute and its functioning. (Para 6.4)
The Committee hopes that position would improve now. (Para 6.5)
The Committee would emphasize that procedural formalities for the centre should be
expedited so as to complete it by the targeted date. (Para 6.6)
The Committee also takes note of major new initiatives for which plans were under
preparation during 2007-08 as listed below:—
➢➢➢➢➢ Construction of new PC Block
➢➢➢➢➢ Advance facilities for Paediatrics (Medical) and (Surgery)
➢➢➢➢➢ Advance facilities for Geriatrics
➢➢➢➢➢ Facility for Family Medicine and Public Health (Para 6.7)
The Committee finds that another set of new projects has been listed to be taken
during 2008-09. The Committee strongly feels that new initiatives should be taken up with
priority being fixed for the most needed ones. The Committee would appreciate if these
initiatives do not continue to be on paper during 2008-09. The Committee recommends that
funds provided for the AIIMS in the Eleventh Plan show both optimum and judicious
utilization as per the action plan with additional provision as and when required. The
Committee is of the view that an effective monitoring mechanism to be effected by all
concerned both at the institute and the Ministry level needs to be in place for the purpose
at the earliest. (Para 6.8)
The Committee expresses deep concern that in the premier institute of the country
like AIIMS so many posts are lying vacant. In the opinion of the Committee, this is
definitely bound to affect the quality of services rendered by the Institute. The Committee,
therefore, recommends immediate action to fill up the vacant posts. (Para 6.9)
The Committee strongly feels that position is bound to aggravate further specially in
view of increasing number of doctors and nurses leaving the institute in the recent years.
The rate of exodus of doctors and nurses from the Institute is a cause of serious concern.
The Department needs to devise a strategy immediately to arrest this trend. The Committee
would like to be informed of the remedial steps taken in this regard. (Para 6.10)
The Committee is deeply concerned about the matter as the Institute is one of the
best training grounds for the doctors and that too at highly subsidized rates involving
precious tax payers’ money. The Committee is of the view that this brain drain is on two
counts-higher studies and lucrative assignments. At the same time, the Committee is also
of the opinion that some policy or enactment should be made so that tendency of leaving
the Institute by doctors/nurses can be minimized. This could be in the form of a monetary
bond or post qualification compulsory service. The Committee strongly feels that urgent
steps are required to be taken so as to ensure an ideal working environment for our young
talented doctors along with all the incentives comparable to those enjoyed by private sector

79
doctors to the extent possible. The Committee would like to be apprised of the steps taken
in this regard which should not be only AIIMS specific but should also cover all the
Government medical institutions. (Para 6.11)
The Committee is given to understand that the Valiathan Committee had submitted
its report on the functioning of AIIMS more than a year ago. The Committee is surprised
to note that only follow up action taken so far is a meeting held under the Chairmanship
of Secretary (Health and Family Welfare) with Director, AIIMS on the 1st March, 2008. The
Committee was informed that the matter was now under Government’ s consideration. The
Committee is not happy with the undue delay in the implementation of Valiathan
Committee recommendations. Any further delay would simply negate the very purpose for
setting up such a Committee, that too at the directive of the Prime Minister. The
Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department to expedite the implementation of the
Valiathan Committee Report. (Para 6.12)
The Committee can only hope that the Burns Unit duly approved will be made
operational by the targeted date. (Para 6.13)

premier Institute of the country, inspite of availability of funds. The Committee has been
informed that an Expenditure Finance Committee proposal for re-development of the

development plan and the circumstances leading to the monitoring of the development of
the Institute by the Jharkhand High Court. (Para 9.3)
X. V ALLABHBHAI PATEL CHEST INSTITUTE, DELHI
The Committee is not aware about the details of developmental projects -both
ongoing and proposed, to be taken up during the Eleventh Plan period. The Committee
would like to be informed of the activities along with the developmental plans of the
Institute for which the funds have been proposed for the Eleventh Plan. (Para 10.2)
The Committee observes that the reply seeking for the details of the short-term
training courses/workshops in respiratory diseases for faculty members and medical
practitioners conducted by the Institute during 2007-08 is not very specific. The Committee
would like to be informed of the same along with proposed workshops, courses etc. in
2008-09. (Para 10.3)
XI. PRADHAN MANTRI SWASTHYA SURAKSHA YOJANA (PMSSY)
The Committee in its 22nd Report on the Demands for Grants (2007-08) presented
on 3rd May, 2007 had expressed its apprehension that it would take at least another plan
period before the six AIIMS like Institutions would start functioning in the real sense. The
Committee is constrained to modify its assessment. From the details made available to the
Committee, construction work on the six AIIMS like Institutions is expected to start by
August-September, 2008 and would be completed in 24 months. Thus, it is more than clear
now that only buildings would be ready by the end of Eleventh Plan. The real target of
making available best health care services to public through these institutions seems to be
a distant dream even now. The Committee finds that tendering process for procurement of
medical equipments is at an initial stage. Process for other allied infrastructure facilities
and manpower-both highly qualified/technical as well as non-technical is yet to start. With
regard to upgradation of 13 Medical College Institutions, the Committee can only hope that
work would be completed within the targeted date of 20 months. The Committee is,
however, worried about the fate of upgradation of Grants Medical College and JJ hospital,

82
Mumbai due to a court case pending in Nagpur High Court in the matter. The Committee
is of the view that the Department should take up other linked activities like arranging for
the faculty and the other requisite infrastructure simultaneously so that no delay takes
place in operationalization of the Institutions once the construction activity is completed.
(Para 11.6)
The Committee also recommends that funds as and when required should be made
available to the Department. The Committee would however like to point out that though
funds have never been a problem for this ambitious project of national importance,
utilization thereof has been far from satisfactory level. The Committee, accordingly,
recommends setting up of a joint mechanism of Centre and the concerned States so that
greater coordination is achieved and effective monitoring of the ongoing projects is done.
The Committee also calls for greater emphasis on adhering to the time lines so that the
overall cost of the project is not escalated further. (Para 11.7)
The Committee, during the oral evidence of the Secretary had taken a serious view
of the delay in implementation of the project. The Committee, therefore, desires the
Department to apprise it of the progress made in implementation of the project, after every
two months. (Para 11.8)
XII. IMPROVEMENT OF NURSING SERVICES
However, the Committee is surprised to observe unsatisfactory level of achievement
under the quantifiable deliverables/physical outputs set for 2007-08. The first target set was
training of 8000 nursing personnel through 48 identified Nursing Institutions. By the end
of the year, no progress seems to have been made from the details made available to the
Committee. Proposal for conducting 78 courses for training of 2340 nurses was under
process. Training of additional 1600 nurses depended upon proposals to be received from the
Institutions. The Committee has been informed that out of 30 institutions, funds could be
released for strengthening of 23 institutions. Status of these institutions is, however, not-
known. The Committee would also like to point out that projects like upgradation of RAK
College of Nursing into Centre of Excellence, upgradation of School of Nursing into College
of Nursing at Dr. RML Hospital, Safdarjung Hospital and Lady Harding Medical College and
establishing a College of Nursing in JIPMER, Puducherry have been there for the last few
years with no evidence of progress being made. Only exception is College of Nursing
at Lady Harding Medical College reported to have started functioning in 2007. The
Committee hopes that required manpower and infrastructure has been made available there.
(Para 12.2)
The Committee is not very hopeful as upgradation of School of Nursing at Dr. RML
Hospital has also been listed as one of the targets to be achieved during 2008-09. The
Committee would like to reiterate that all these projects need to be closely monitored so
as to ensure their completion within the time schedule without any cost escalation in the
original estimate. The Department should not be a mere spectator, it should devise some
mechanism for proper utilization of the funds and its repeated contention that the
utilization/grants of funds depends upon receipt of SOE/UCs is not acceptable to the
Committee. The Department has to play a more proactive roles in co-ordination with the
hospital/college authorities. The problem areas wherever noticed need to be removed at the
earliest. (Para 12.3)
The Committee is not aware about the existence of any Monitoring Committee for
such projects. The Committee is of the view that such a mechanism will prove to be very
useful, especially in view of Rs.198.00 crore allocated for strengthening/upgradation of

83
Nursing Services. The Committee welcomes the enhancement in the assistance to be
provided to Nursing Institutions from Rs.10.00 lakhs to Rs.25.00 lakhs. Such a move was
over due. The Committee, however, wonders whether any exercise has been initiated for
identification of locations of all the proposed Centres/Schools/Colleges so far. The
Committee would appreciate if implementation of all these projects is carried out in a time-
bund manner. The Committee is not aware about any assessment/review made recently
about the (training both pre and in-service) programmes for Nurses and also functioning of
Training Institutions for Nurses. The Committee is of the view that such an exercise is
necessary for strengthening the Nursing Services which is a very crucial component of
health care. (Para 12.4)
The Committee is happy to note that the National Awards for Nurses, given as a
mark of highest recognition for the meritorious services of the nurses and nursing
profession in the country, that continued up to 1989, have been revived and named as the
National Florence Nightingale Award from 2007 with the consent of the President of India.
17 Nursing personnel have been awarded with this prestigious award during the year 2007.
(Para 12.5)
The Committee recommends that a suitable mechanism should be evolved for
maintaining a live register of nurses so as to enable the Department for formulating
appropriate policy pertaining to nurses. (Para 12.6)
The Committee recommends that the Department should make all out efforts
including effective co-ordination and close monitoring so that all the proposals for
strengthening of nursing education are implemented properly and desired results
are achieved for getting adequate number of qualified and trained nursing personnel.
(Para 12.7)
While appreciating the initiatives, the Committee would like to point out that out of
total nursing strength of 3015 in Central Government Hospitals in Delhi, only 795 nursing
personnel have been provided with accommodation. If such unsatisfactory conditions are in
Delhi, the Committee can well imagine the conditions in State Government Hospitals. The
Committee strongly feels that residential facilities for Nurses need to be augmented at the
earliest. The Committee recommends the Department to formulate a comprehensive policy
to stop exodus of nurses as also to offer more incentives so as to make the profession more
attractive for arresting this trend. (Para 12.9)
XIII. UPGRADATION OF DIS TRICT HOSPITALS
The Committee welcomes the initiative of the Department for upgradation of the
District Hospitals. While recommending priority to the remote and rural area hospitals and
those States where MMR and IMR are high and where maternity facilities are not up to the
mark, the Committee would recommend formulating a mechanism so as to facilitate early
selection, granting and overseeing proper utilization of funds. The Committee would also
emphasize that all efforts should be made to fully utilize the approved outlay of Rs. 1500.00
crores for the Eleventh Plan. For this, targets need to be set and all hurdles in
implementation need to be removed. The Committee has in the past witnessed that funds
could not be utilized optimally and many schemes could not achieve desired success for want
of proposals, submission of utilization certificates from State Governments etc. The
Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to expedite scrutiny of the proposals
received from the State Governments from the beginning of financial year 2008-09 itself.
(Para 13.2)

84
XIV . RASHTRIYA AROGYA NIDHI
The Committee observes that even after more than a decade of setting up of the
fund with 50% of the contribution made by the State/UT to be provided by Central
Government, there are still several States/UTs which have not set up the State Illness
Assistance Fund. Every State/UTs should have such a fund. The Committee would appreciate
if this matter is taken up at the highest level in all such State/UTs. (Para 14.3)
The Committee feels that in order to facilitate easy access to quality health care to
the poor and downtrodden strata of our society, the limit of Rs. 50,000 under immediate
financial assistance funds, per case, for which funds are placed at the disposal of Medical
Superintendents of above hospitals, need to be enhanced realistically for treatment of
dreaded diseases like AIDS, Cancer etc. Some of the major States like U.P., Assam,
Karnataka, Kerala and Jammu & Kashmir do not have such a fund. With only a very few
major hospitals located in metros having extended facility under the fund, people of such
States/UTs are being deprived of medical care for no fault of theirs. From the details of
funds released to States/UTs during 2005-08, it is very clear that such States are having
negligible funds at their disposal. The Committee wonders about the adequacy of such State
funds. The Committee is of the view that with the increasing rate of inflation and also
increasing number of patients suffering from major diseases, an assessment of the
Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi should be made at the earliest. Necessary changes may be made
thereafter. The facility of financial assistance should be extended in more hospitals so as
to cover the geographical limits of the country. The Committee also recommends to the
Department to give wide publicity to the scheme specially in the hospital campuses
to generate awareness so that the same can be utilized by the needy and poor patients.
(Para 14.4)
XV. NATIONAL URBAN HEALTH MISSION (NUHM)
The Committee observes that NUHM is one of the most ambitious Projects after
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM). Objectives of the Mission are laudable and are
according to the requirements of the present scenario. The Committee cautions the
Department to take all necessary steps so that the problems afflicting the implementation
of NRHM like those related to ground level healthcare functionaries, availability of doctors,
paramedics and infrastructure do not recur and interfere in the implementation of parallel
scheme meant for urban areas. For achieving the targets proposed under mission the
Department should do proper homework and work out modalities for their implementation.
The Department should start coordinating with the States right from the beginning of the
project. The Committee would like to be apprised about the progress made in this regard.
(Para 15.4)
XVI. NATIONAL AIDS CONTROL PROGRAMME (NACP)
The Committee is constrained to note that against a Plan provision of
Rs.815.00 crore which was increased to Rs.953.89 crore at the RE stage during 2007-08 for
NACP, expenditure reported upto 13th Mar ch, 2008 was only Rs.767.34 crore. The
Committee observes that optimum utilization has not been achieved in any of the
components of NACO. The Committee notes that the Department has not been able to
achieve optimum utilization of funds during 2006-07 also. The Committee  was given to
understand that procedural delays in the procurement of equipment and non-utilization of
funds placed at the disposal of other Ministries like Ministry of Social Justice and
Empowerment and Information and Broadcasting were the main factors for under-

85
utilization of allocated funds during 2006-07. The Committee is afraid that similar reasons
would be given for 2007-08 also. It seems that weekly monitoring meetings at NACO level
and quarterly monitoring meetings with the State SACs followed by visits of teams of
officers to the States to ascertain the progress of work and level of expenditure have failed
to make any noticeable improvement. In view of enhanced allocation of Rs. 1100.00 crore
made for 2008-09, the Committee recommends to the Department to take immediate
corrective measures and make every conceivable effort so as to ensure optimum and
judicious utilization of funds. (Para 16.5)
The Committee is dismayed to note that progress made under several components of
the programme is abysmal and the trend has been continuing irrespective of the issue being
raised again and again. The Committee has been viewing with serious concern the trend of
targets remaining under-achieved in the past few years. Last year, the Committee was given
to understand that non-procurement of blood bank equipment seriously hampered the
modernization of District Level Blood Banks. Non-availability of STD specialists and
specialized STD services were held responsible for target set for STD clinics. The Committee
has been given to understand that instead of the previous emphasis on opening of STD
facilities, now targets are being set for the number of STD cases treated. The Committee
would, however, like to point out that readjustments of targets will not result in having the
required STD specialists and services. The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation
of formulating a comprehensive plan for the training of doctors in handling AIDS cases. The
Committee recommends to the Department to inform it about the major problem areas in
the implementation of National AIDS Control Programme and the corrective measures
taken/ proposed by the Department to overcome the same. (Para 16.6)
The Committee would recommend to the Department to continue its consultations
with the States that have either suspended or banned the programme and achieve consensus
in implementing the scheme. (Para 16.7)
The Committee appreciates these priorities of the Department and recommends the
Department to inform it about the specific steps to be taken by it for achievement of the
same. (Para 16.8)
The Committee is happy to note that though delayed, the Department has taken the
desired step towards starting the second line of treatment to lessen the sufferings of drug
resistant patients. The Committee would like to recommend to the Department to put in
place an effective mechanism so that no patient in need of second line ART is deprived of
it. (Para 16.10)
The Committee is not fully inclined to agree with the contention of the Ministry.
Some of the corrective measures in centralized procurement as mentioned below clearly
indicate that besides deficiencies at the State level, implementation at the Central level was
also not upto the mark:—
➢➢➢➢➢ Procurement responsibility shifted from Procurement Support Agencies to the
United Nations Office for Project Services for Bank supported operations.
➢➢➢➢➢ Creation of Financial Management Group at the Health Ministry.
➢➢➢➢➢ Development of detailed guidelines and operational manuals for procurement of
NGOs and Public Private Partnerships.
➢➢➢➢➢ Introduction of evaluation of NGO performance by Committee having one
external evaluator.

86
➢➢➢➢➢ Termination of contracts of about 25% NGOs.
➢➢➢➢➢ Pre-award validation/certification of WHO GMP made mandatory in all cases.
(Para 16.12)
From the information available with the Committee, it notes that services of as
many as 177 NGOs have been discontinued. Besides that 48 Community Care Centres being
run by NGOs have been discontinued after on site evaluation. The Committee is dismayed
at the fact that an alarming percentage of NGOs were blacklisted and had to be removed.
The Committee is not inclined to admit that the whole problem was at the district level of
officials. The Committee opines that either this is a case of poor monitoring mechanism at
the Department level or there is more to the matter than what is visible. The Committee
would like to have a Status Note on the performance of NGOs, unspent balances available
with the blacklisted NGOs and action taken for the recovery of the same. Details of all
similar cases/discrepancies related to NACO and the action taken by the Department/CBI
in that regard may also be furnished to the Committee. (Para 16.13)
XVII. NATIONAL CANCER CONTROL PROGRAMME (NCCP)
Against a Tenth Plan allocation of Rs.333.00 crore, enhanced provision of
Rs.2871.92 crore including a provision of Rs.471.92 crore for tobacco control has been made
for the Eleventh Plan. While welcoming this initiative of the Government, the Committee
is constrained to point out that level of utilization has to keep pace with the enhanced
provision. The Committee has been persistently highlighting the need for better
management and co-ordination of all concerned. However, the position remains unchanged.
Against the Tenth Plan allocation of Rs. 333.00 crore, utilization reported at the end of the
year was only Rs.252.95 crore. The Committee finds that year 2007-08, which is the
first year of the Eleventh Plan failed to bring any improvement. Plan allocation of
Rs.140.00 crores for 2007-08 for the NCCP was reduced to Rs.70.00 crores at the RE stage.
The expenditure reported up to 29.02.08 is only Rs.40.31 crores. Similarly, plan provision of
Rs.40.00 crore for tobacco control had to be brought down to Rs.29.00 crore with utilization
of only Rs.7.63 crore by 29.02.2008. (Para 17.3)
The Committee takes a serious view of total lack of initiative on the part of the
Department so far as implementation of National Cancer Control Programme is concerned.
The Committee strongly feels that its following observations made in the 25th report have
failed to make any impact on the Department:—
“The Committee is not satisfied with the citing of a number of procedural formalities
as the major factor for undue delay in the release of funds by the Department. It
is for the Department to take a pro-active role by pursuing with State Governments
for sending viable proposals. As admitted by the Department, the proposal for up-
gradation of nine existing RCCs into Centre of Excellence was considered only during
the last quarter of the year and five institutions were approved for funding. However,
due to non-availability of required funds, only four institutions could be funded.
What is more disturbing is that the entire allocation of Rs. 8.70 crore earmarked for
NE Region remained unutilised for want of complete proposals. Keeping in view the
experience of 2006-07, the Committee recommends to the Department to put in place
an effective monitoring mechanism for implementation of Cancer Control
Programme.”
It is a sorry state of affairs that at the end of the year, a large number of proposals
received for different components were at a ripe stage but due to paucity of time and some

87
technical deficiency found in the proposals, the same could not be materialized. It is high
time that an effective monitoring mechanism in co-ordination with all the implementing
agencies is put in place without any further delay. (Para 17.5)
The Committee observes that achievement of these targets will depend to a large
extent on the finalization, of EFC for the Eleventh Plan which proposes substantial increase
in the grant-in-aid. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that efforts may be made to
obtain the EFC approval at the earliest. It has also been proposed to enter into new phase
of Public Private Partnership which also required enhanced grant-in-aid. The Committee
would like to be apprised about the details of this new component. As commented in the
previous para, the Committee once again enjoins upon the Department to enhance its
efforts from the beginning of this financial year and take suitable corrective measures
including strict monitoring so that the approved outlay for NCCP is properly and optimally
utilized. (Para 17.6)
The Committee recommends to the Department to take up its case more vigorously
and with sound reasoning with the State Government of West Bengal for early handing over
the piece of land for early construction of the campus of CNCI, Kolkata. (Para 17.7)
Committee feels that some corrective measures need to be taken by the Department
for submission of UCs by the State Governments under NCCP. Depar tment being a nodal
agency, should make all efforts so that funds allocated are in no way allowed to go
unutilized for want of proposals and submission of UCs. As far as non submission of
utilization certificates is concerned, the Committee feels that there could be possibilities of
diversion of the funds. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department has to
ensure timely submission of UCs. The Committee would appreciate if a Status Note on
pending UCs (State/NGO-wise) is submitted to it. (Para 17.8)
The Committee recommends to the Department to give utmost priority to evaluation
of the National Cancer Control Programme by a premier agency having experience of
work in such Disease Control Programmes. Proper evaluation would help in identifying
weak links and result in effective implementation of various components of the programme.
(Para 17.9)
XVIII. NATIONAL TOBACCO CONTROL PROGRAMME (NTCP)
The Committee was informed last year that the ‘in principle’ approval of the
Planning Commission for setting up of the National Regulatory Authority and Referral Labs
for testing Tar and Nicotine content in various tobacco products has been obtained. Process
for seeking approval of the competent authority had already begun at that time. The
Committee, however, notes that no progress seems to have been made in this regard
thereafter. Keeping in view the prolonged process of getting the approval of the competent
authority, the Committee does not have much hope about the same being obtained by June,
2008. The Department has to make concerted efforts so that approval of the competent
authority for setting up of the National Regulatory Authority, backbone of the entire
programme is obtained at the earliest. (Para 18.4)
More than one million people are dying due to consumption of tobacco in the country.
The Committee, therefore, strongly feels that the Ministry needs to bring up sustained
Mass Media/IEC campaign regarding the adverse and harmful effects of tobacco
consumption immediately, as also when NTCP is launched. Sufficient funds should be made
available for the same. (Para 18.5)

88
XIX. NATIONAL MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAMME (NMHP)
The Committee is constrained to note that in spite of approved outlay being
drastically reduced to nearly half for the National Mental Health Programme, the
expenditure reported upto 29th February, 2008 is a meager Rs.14.13 crores. A proposal for
releasing funds to the extent of Rs.22.165 crore (including Rs.4.71 crore for NE) was stated
to be under consideration. The Committee takes a serious view of the continuing trend of
poor utilization of funds earmarked for the programme. (Para 19.4)
The Committee is dismayed at the fact that the expansion of the National Mental
Health Programme envisaged for the Eleventh Plan is yet to be approved. The Committee
recommends the Department to present its case strongly and effectively so as to get
necessary approval without further delay. Further, the Department can not simply shy away
from its responsibility by stating that progress of the events in these schemes depends on
the active cooperation of the State Governments and other stake holders. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends the Department to approach and have regular interactions with the
State Governments concerned and identify the problem areas which need to be addressed.
The Department should be proactive so as to motivate the State Governments to participate
in the programme actively and furnish proposals with all requisite information to enable
release and utilization of the funds optimally. The Committee would like to be informed of
the remedial measures taken by the Department in this regard. (Para 19.6)
The Committee would like to point out that majority of districts in the country
continue to remain outside the purview of District Mental Health Programme. Only 100
districts have been covered so far, with another 125 new districts proposed to be brought
under the programme during 2008-09. The Committee would like to emphasize that all the
districts need to be covered at the earliest. All efforts need to be made in this direction.
(Para 19.8)
XX. NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF DIABETES,
CARDIOV ASCULAR DISEASES STROKE (NPDCS)
The Committee is happy to note that the pilot phase of the programme has finally
taken off during 2007-08. (Para 20.4)
The Committee notes that out of an approved outlay of Rs. 1660.50 crores for the
Eleventh Five Year Plan, only Rs.30.00 crores have been earmarked for 2008-09. This, when
taken into account along with last year’s utilization of Rs.4.42 crore, leaves behind a
whopping amount of Rs.1625.50 crores for the last three years of the Plan. The Committee
is given to understand that a Steering Committee has been established to review and
expedite the Programme. A meeting of the States participating in the pilot project was held
on 17th October, 2007. Appreciating this initiative, the Committee recommends to the
Department to carry forward the programme vigorously during the remaining period of the
Plan so that the set targets are achieved with the optimum utilization of funds available for
the programme. (Para 20.5)
XXI. MEDICAL EDUCATION
The Committee is aware that keeping in view the shortage of doctors and existing
medical institutions not being adequate enough, MCI norms for opening of colleges/increase
of seats need to be reviewed. The Committee, however, feels that this exercise should be
undertaken with extreme caution and objective of imparting quality medical education
remaining intact. Relaxing norms by allowing private promoters to have land in two pieces

89
within 10 Kms. of each other and allowing corporate entities to setup medical colleges are
initiatives which should be implemented after examining all pros and cons. The Committee
is of the opinion that in the exercise of relaxation of existing norms, assessment of those
experts having the experience of this field should be given due weightage. (Para 21.4)
The Committee also takes note of the suggestion of the Department to MCI for
relaxing the age of retirement of staff of private medical educational institutes from 65 to
70 years, subject to their physical ability, in order to fill-up the acute shortage of teaching
staff in that sector. Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare has also informed
the Committee that a Cabinet Note has been prepared for increasing the age of retirement
to 65 years in Government Medical Educational Institutes. Committee is also given to
understand that PG degrees of USA, UK, Australia, New Zealand and Canada have been
recognized and for other countries like Germany and France the matter is under
consideration. The idea is that they can come and settle here or they can come as visiting
faculties. The Committee welcomes these steps. (Para 21.5)
On being asked as to whether any mechanism was in place to check this, the
Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare stated that at present there is no
mechanism to prevent Indian students from going abroad to study. The Committee is of the
view that the Department needs to devise an effective mechanism, which could include a
legislation, so that Indian medical students can be prevented from going to such places
whose educational system does not match with ours. The Committee would like to be
informed about the steps taken by the Department in this regard. (Para 21.6)
The Committee is anguished to note that the fate of so many students of the
remaining 18 medical colleges, who have already appeared in their final examination,
remains undecided. The Committee is of the view that the students should not suffer due
to such technicalities and bureaucratic hurdles. A decision without any further delay may
be taken in the matter. A Status Note on such colleges may also be submitted to the
Committee. (Para 21.7)
The Committee opines that if implemented, the recommendations of the Commission
would be a milestone in improving the standards and quality of medical education in India.
The Committee recommends action may be initiated in this regard and Committee apprised
accordingly. (Para 21.9)
XXII. V ACANCIES IN CGHS CADRE
The Committee is constrained to observe that the Department was able to achieve
little progress in filling up the vacant posts during the last one year. As informed to this
Committee the joining rate of the GDMOs is very less. The Committee, therefore,
recommends the Department to enhance its efforts in the right direction by identifying the
problem areas and devising a strategy to counter such problems in all sub-cadre posts at the
earliest. The Committee would like to be informed about the steps taken by it to fill up
vacancies in the different sub-cadres. (Para 22.2)
Now that the Sixth Pay Commission has submitted its recommendations, the
Committee would recommend to the Department to expedite the implementation of the
Javed Chaudhary Committee recommendations. The Committee would like to be informed
of the progress made in this regard. (Para 22.3)
The Committee views with serious concern the grave injustice done to the GDMO
cadre for no fault of theirs. Inspite of their being eligible for specialist post, continuance
of such doctors in GDMO cadre is indeed against all principles of natural justice. Non-

90
implementation of Fifth Pay Commission recommendation of SAG level positions in All
India Service to be 17% of total cadre has created another hurdle in their career
progression. The Committee finds that Sixth Pay Commission recommendation of filling up
the additional posts to be created for fulfilling any gap by direct recruitment will make the
position of GDMOs very vulnerable. The Committee is of the firm opinion that the
Department should take up this issue immediately with the Ministry of Finance. Every
attempt should be made to remove the grave injustice done to the GDMO cadre so that this
sub-cadre of professionals gets due recognition and morale boost like others in All India
services. (Para 22.5)
XXIII. NEW SCHEMES
The Committee is dismayed to note that every year the Department announces new
schemes/programmes, many of which are without finalizing the modalities and proper
ground work, thereby resulting in under or no utilization of funds. The Committee
recommends to the Department to enhance its efforts to complete all necessary formalities
and launch the programmes at the earliest so that funds do not get blocked in such
schemes. (Para 23.2)
XXIV. MISCELLANEOUS
The Committee recommends the Department to take care of the eco-friendly part of
the whole exercise. (Para 24.1)
The Committee recommends the Department to work out modalities for establishing
specialized kidney centres immediately and in the meantime approach the Planning
Commission for funds with a proposal to improve dialysis facility in the country. In view
of increasing gap in demand and supply, at least the well known Institutes across India
should be provided with the dialysis machines during the current financial year. The
Committee would like to be informed about the steps taken by the Department in this
regard. (Para 24.2)

requirement of health infrastructure in the country. In a vast country like ours, rigid
norms based on population only and made uniformly applicable were perhaps not proving to
be justified and not based on ground realities. The Committee is also of the view that
change in the norms for health infrastructure proposed by the Planning Commission was
called for. The Committee is, however, not aware whether any preparatory exercise has been
initiated for conducting surveys as per the revised norms. The Committee is afraid that if
this issue is allowed to linger on for long, the very objective of NRHM of bridging gaps in
the health care will continue to be a distant dream. The Committee, accordingly, impresses

The Committee is happy to note the progr ess made by the Depar tment on the ASHA

– advising newly married couples for their special needs.
– guiding pregnant women for availing of institutional facilities for Anti-Natal,

– counselling on nutrition, pregnancy, breast-feeding, immunization and family
planning.
– establishing link with PHCs, private providers and others for service requirement
of beneficiaries.
– mobilising parents for child survival interventions.
– promoting basic sanitization.
– provision of non-clinical spacing contraceptives.
– surveillance of communicable diseases. (Para 3.12)

responsibilities entrusted to  the ASHA. As the initiative is still in the early stages, the
