IV. NATIONAL VECTOR BORNE DISEASE CONTROL PROGRAMME (NVBDCP)
The Committee notes that like in the previous years, funds provided in 2007-08
remained under-utilised. Expenditure reported upto 29.02.08 is Rs.283.74 crore. Secretary,
while deposing before the Committee had mentioned that by 31.03.2008, expenditure figures
stood at Rs.385.38 crore, indicating 96.46% utilisation of allocated funds of Rs.399.50 crore.
The Committee is constrained to point out that instead of there being an improvement,
position has worsened in 2007-08. An amount of Rs.102.00 crore being spent in the last
month of the financial year calls for serious introspection. The Committee has been
repeatedly impressing upon the Department for initiating corrective measures in this
regard. Reasons like delay in procurement process, submission of SOE/UCs by States/UTs
and non-recruitment of required staff seem to have persisted in 2007-08 also. (Para 4.2)
The Committee strongly feels that mere chalking out an elaborate Action Plan and
allocation of funds for control of a major disease does not seem to make any sense if year
after year same constraints seem to persist. The Committee once again tries to impress
upon the Department to take immediate steps for removal of bottlenecks in the successful
implementation of Malaria Control Programme. The Committee would like to mention
that under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, major component is
Malaria Control having the maximum allocation of Rs.351.68 crore out of a provision of
Rs.440.03 crores for the entire programme in 2008-09. Therefore, it is in the fitness of
things that concerted efforts are also made for optimum and judicious utilisation of
allocated funds. (Para 4.3)
The Committee is alarmed by the trend of Pf cases reported from these States.
Committee’s attention has also been drawn to quantum jump of number of malaria deaths
reported in the country. In 2006,1639 deaths were reported against 963 deaths occurring in
2005. By November, 2007, this figure has already reached 807. The Committee has every
reason to apprehend that actual figures of deaths may be higher than what is officially
recorded. Reason being there is no mechanism at present to independently verify the field
level figures for any State. (Para 4.5)

97
The Committee has been persistently drawing the attention of the Department to the
urgent need for implementation of all malaria control measures in Malaria endemic States
of NE Region, Orissa and West Bengal. The Committee is well aware that NE States
together contribute 4% of the country’s population, 12% of malaria cases, 18% of Pf cases
and 54% of the total malaria related deaths reported in the country during 2006. Figures
must have remained unchanged in 2007 also. Another  cause of concern is increasing trend
of resistance to conventional anti-malarial drug Chloroquine noticed in NE States. The
Committee notes that Global Fund supported Intensified Malaria Control Project in NE
States being implemented since July, 2005 with a contribution of US $ 30 million for
the first two years of the project also seems to have failed to have the desired impact.
(Para 4.6)
The Committee notes that increased supervision and monitoring is one of the main
strategies adopted for effective control of malaria. The latest figures made available to the
Committee reveal continuance of shortage of surveillance and supervisory staff in NE States.
In Assam, the biggest State of NE Region, against the sanctioned posts of 694 Health
Supervisor (Male) only 570 were in position, against 343 Health Supervisor (Female), there
were 316 and only 1647 MPW(M) against 3080 sanctioned posts. What is more disturbing is
that while Tripura failed to furnish the data, Meghalaya and Nagaland have provided
incomplete information. The primary role of MPW (M) and MPW (F) is door to door
surveillance and detection of communicable diseases and it’s reporting. The fact that these
functionaries play a vital role in disease detection and surveillance cannot be ignored. By not
appointing these functionaries, the States leave a big gap at the field-level disease
surveillance, detection and treatment. This vital issue needs to be pursued at the highest level
in the concerned States. The other strategy adopted is use of Rapid Diagnostic Kits by ASHAs.
The Committee does not have high expectation from this initiative as firstly required number
of ASHAs have to be in place in malaria endemic States and even if they are there, they
would be over-burdened with the various tasks already assigned to them. The Committee fails
to comprehend the continuance of such a discouraging situation inspite of special dispensation
for NE States. The Committee can only reiterate that there is need for drastic measures and
extensive monitoring under the supervision of State Nodal Officers. (Para 4.7)
Kala-azar
The Committee strongly feels that effective surveillance, timely treatment and
compliance of treatment regimens in all PHCs would lead to better reports in 2008. The
Committee is of the view that only if intensive monitoring at all levels is carried out, the
goal of elimination of Kala-azar by 2010 can be made achievable. Situation so far has not
been very encouraging. All the quantifiable objectives listed in the Action Plan for 2008-09
need to be closely monitored on monthly basis. (Para 4.9)
Japanese Encephalitis
The Committee is dismayed to note that despite various methods adopted by the
Department over the past year to contain the disease, the number of cases reported to be
suffering from JE/AES has shown an increase over the previous year figures. The fact is
even more disturbing that though the Department claims to have completed 99.97%
immunization in the past year in 7 worst affected districts in Uttar Pradesh, the situation
there has worsened with 2675 cases and 577 deaths in 2007 (till December) over the 2006
figures of 2320 cases and 528 deaths. The Committee fails to comprehend as to why inspite
of a number of preventive measures taken by the Central Government in co-ordination with
the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, the JE/AES related cases and deaths continue to

98
be high in the State. The Committee apprehends that the actual figures would increase the
tally much further. The Committee would like to take the opportunity to State that though
the data for Assam has not been made available by the Department, going by the fact sheet
of 2006, it is apprehensive that the situation in Assam would also show a similar trend as
that of U.P. (Para 4.10)
The Committee would like to draw the attention of the Department to the fact that
the year 2006 had reported a visible impact of preventive measures initiated by registering
a declining trend when compared with 2005 figures. Quantum jump in the first three
quarter of 2007 calls for a serious review with special focus on Assam and U.P., the two
main endemic States. The Committee would impress upon the Department that analysis of
epidemiological and entomological data for epidemic outbreak prediction and timely remedial
measures is required to be carried out on an urgent basis.
The Committee feels that perhaps the precautionary methods adopted by the
Department have not percolated properly to the affected population because of which the
disease has once again registered an increase. The Committee adds that lax monitoring of
the disease by the central as well as the State Government could aggravate the situation
further unless it is dealt with a sense of urgency. It suggests the Department to undertake
on-the-spot review of the situation as to the possible causes for upsurge in the reported
cases. The Committee urges the Department to step-up the ongoing IEC activities in the
endemic States so that the desired objective is reached soon. (Para 4.11)
Dengue/Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever/Chikungunya
Incidence of Chikungunya cases in the country during 2006 and 2007 has led the
Committee to the conclusion that various initiatives taken by the Department have so far
failed to yield any desired results. The Committee strongly feels that with the enhanced
allocation of Rs.14.59 crore in 2008-09 for Dengue and Chikungunya, effective measures are
required to be undertaken in the affected States. Mere circulation of detailed guidelines and
advisories for prevention and control of these diseases to all affected States would not serve
any purpose. What is required is to identify the affected districts and go for regular fever
surveillance in such endemic areas to detect an unusual trend. The Committee is of the
view that if this analysis of ground reality is followed by IEC activities and strengthening
of apex Referral Institutions for diagnosis and treatment, number of Dengue/Chikungunya
cases would show a declining trend. The Committee apprehends that unless adequate
remedial measures are taken, sporadic outburst of these diseases would continue to be
reported from different States every year. (Para 4.17)
V. NATIONAL T. B. CONTROL PROGRAMME
The Committee appreciates the successful implementation of RNTCP Phase-I and
ongoing Phase-II. Several initiatives/interventions taken at different levels and variety of
implementing agencies have contributed to the increasing population coverage and 85% cure
rate. However, India still contributes 20% of TB cases reported in the world. Out of 8.8
million cases per annum, 1.8 million cases are from India alone. New complex off shoots of
TB also keep on emerging, the most visible being worsening HIV epidemic increasing the
number of TB cases. The Committee notes that HIV is the most potent risk factor for
progression of TB infection to disease form. HIV-TB patients detected in 2005 were 12,062,
13,614 in 2006 and 18,559 in 2007. The Committee is aware that increase in number of
co-infected (HIV-TB) patients being detected over the last three years is a result of innovative
and co-ordinated measures taken by the Department. But the other dimension of this trend

99
is increasing complexities involved in the treatment of such cases. The Committee hopes that
the National Framework formulated by RNTCP and NACP for joint TB/HIV collaborative
activities will lead to better and effective control of this emerging problem area. (Para 5.4)
The Committee observes that the other major challenge to TB control in the country
is increasing number of MDR- TB cases. The Committee is aware that such cases are bound
to increase the magnitude and severity of TB epidemic and pose a major threat to TB
control. The Committee in its earlier Report has pointed out that 7% defaulters in a year
is quite a significant number of cases remaining untreated or half-treated. With a single
TB patient infecting 10-15 persons in a year, rate of infection is bound to increase. The
Committee would like to point out that formulation of guidelines for management of MDR
TB cases and publication thereof will not prove to be sufficient enough. The Committee had
given a simple suggestion for identifying the defaulter TB patients from the records being
maintained at centres/hospitals with the help of NGOs/Social Workers and Private
Practitioners. Intention of the Committee was to identify such cases at the first default
stage itself. The Committee finds that under a new initiative a total of 50 MDR- TB patients
were to be registered for treatment in Gujarat and Maharashtra during 2007-08 to be
doubled every year subsequently and ultimately in the entire country. While welcoming this
initiative, the Committee would also like to point out that cost of MDR- TB treatment is
300 times more than non-MDR TB. The Committee can only say that preventive measures
will be both cost-effective and helpful for the patients. The Committee is of the firm
opinion that through effective IEC activities and alertness of health workers regular intake
of medicines can be easily monitored. The Committee, therefore, suggests that monitoring
of TB patients—the most vital aspect, should not be ignored at any cost. (Para 5.5)

depends on the approval of EFC Memo by the Ministry of Finance and CCEA. Till then, the
funds allocated for 2008-09 will continue to be utilized as per the existing scheme approved
for the Tenth Plan. The Committee is not happy with this state of affairs. Second year of
Eleventh Plan has already started and by the time approval of the competent authority is
finally received, the year 2008-09 would be nearing its end. The Committee would like to
point out that some of the new initiatives like construction of dedicated Eye Wings/Eye
OTs in District Hospitals, appointment of manpower, development of mobile Ophthalmic
Units in NE States will have to undergo a number of procedural formalities before their
actually taking off. The Committee accordingly recommends that concerted efforts need to
be made for getting the formal approval at the earliest. The Committee would appreciate
if simultaneously preparatory activities are also started. (Para 7.4)
The Committee has been taking note of instances of malfunctioning of Eye Camps
reported in the Media in the different States. The Committee feels that monitoring of Eye
Camps is being exclusively done by the District Blindness Control Societies. Department’s
role starts as and when reports regarding malfunctioning of Eye Camps held in States are
brought to the notice of the Ministry. Corrective measures are accordingly taken by the
Ministry. The Committee, however, feels that the Department needs to be more pro-active
in such cases. One corrective measure which can be initiated by the Department without
any special efforts involved is to review the performance of such Eye Camps in the State
level meetings, with required follow-up action taken on the reported incidents of
malfunctioning of Eye Camps. The Committee is also of the view that follow-up treatment
after Eye Camps should be made mandatory and strictly enforced. District hospital

102
authorities also need to be involved in the conducting of such Eye Camps by introduction
of compulsory, pre-checks in Eye Camps before start of Eye surgery and other treatment.
The Committee would like to add here that the Department should also devise some method
of surprise inspection of such eye camps organized by the NGOs to facilitate cataract
operations. This, the Committee feels, would ensure stricter compliance by all the concerned
entities and help reduce eyes mishaps. The Committee notes that the process for
independent evaluation of NPCB including evaluation of work being done by NGOs has been
initiated. The Committee would appreciate if this exercise is expedited so that corrective
measures are taken at the earliest. (Para 7.5)
The Committee is not convinced that the IEC activities are being carried out as
intensely as is stated by the Department. The Committee has been given to understand that
out of the total allocated budget under National Programme for Control of Blindness,
around 7% has been spent on IEC, which according to the Committee, is quite a sizable
amount. The Committee strongly feels that public awareness about the noble cause of eye
donation for blind persons continues to be very low. The Committee is of the view that a
review of IEC activities on this aspect need to be made in consultation with all the stake
holders, specially reputed Eye Hospitals/NGOs doing commendable work in this area and
also both Government and private ad agencies. The Committee would also like to emphasise
that the functioning of Eye Banks in the country requires to be reviewed in view of reported
lack of logistic support for timely collection of eyes by the Eye Banks. Steps also to need
to be taken for increasing the number of Eye Banks in the country. (Para. 7.7)
The Committee notes with disappointment that the target to bring prevalence of
blindness to 0.8% by 2007 has not been reached. The Department has informed that as per
the report of Rapid Survey on Avoidable Blindness (2007), the prevalence of blindness has
come down to 1% and that Cataract remains the single largest cause of blindness, low
vision and one eye blindness in India. The Committee also infers from the above study that
the prevalence of blindness due to Trachoma also continues to be there. It is a well known
fact that blindness is a bane of nature. The Committee believes that most of the people in
smaller towns and rural areas are not aware of the symptoms of the above ailments, and
the methods to manage eye care, their eye-care service seeking behavior pattern do not
change. The Committee exhorts the Department to take all possible necessary steps to
devise IEC activities in local media and television channels so that awareness among the
people is increased. The Committee believes a lot of cases of blindness can be checked by
such a measure and would in the long run help to achieve the targeted goals under the
programme. (Para 7.9)
VIII. NATIONAL IODINE DEFICIENCIES DISORDERS PROGRAMME
The Committee notes with dismay that not even one of the targets set under the
Programme could be achieved during the past year by the given time line. Moreover, uptill
28.2.2008, only Rs.13.13 crores of the funds released, could be spent. The Committee
considers such a trend highly unsatisfactory. The Committee remarking on the under-
utilisation of funds during 2006-07, had expressed its apprehension on proper utilisation of
funds allocated under the Programme for 2007-08 in its 22nd Report. The Committee was
given to understand that a provision of Rs.4.30 crores has been made for States and UTs
to meet the expenditure on the following components for the same year.
1. Establishment of an IDD Control Cell
2. Establishment of an IDD Monitoring Lab
3. DD Surveys/resurveys of districts

103
4. Health Education and Publicity
To the utter dismay of the Committee, the States could not set up even one IDD
Control Cell or IDD Monitoring Lab. Not only that, of the 20,000 salt samples the
Department had planned to analyse from 40 districts at the rate of 500 samples per district,
not even one sample had been analysed. The Committee takes a serious view of this.
The Committee’s attention has also been drawn by enhanced allocation of
Rs.32 crores in 2008-09. The Committee would like to emphasise once again that all
conceivable efforts may be made so as to ensure optimum and judicious utilization of
allocated funds. (Para 8.2)
IX. REPRODUCTIVE AND CHILD HEALTH PROGRAMME
The Committee, however, notes that under RCH Flexible Pool expenditure reported
upto 29th February, 2008 was only Rs.1643.62 crore. Similarly, under the Mission Flexible
Pool, Utilisation status as on 29th February, 2008 as reported in the Outcome Budget was
Rs.2505.05 crore. Spending of major portion of the allocated funds during the last quarter
clearly indicates that both the major programmes continue to have some inherent problem
areas. The assessment of the Committee is confirmed by the performance of High Focus
States during 2007-08 as indicated below:

The Committee feels that monitoring mechanism for such Schemes needs to be very
effective so that no grey areas are there to be misused by unscrupulous persons. The
Committee would like to have a Status Note on the procedure of verification of claims and
release of compensation package under the programme. The Committee also strongly feels
that community participation is encouraged so as to keep a watchful eye on the activities
of Implementing agencies under the Scheme. The Committee would also appreciate if an
assessment is made about the impact of JSY on the lowering of Maternal Mortality Rate
in the crucial States. (Para 9.13)
ROUTINE IMMUNISATION PROGRAMME
The Committee has been observing that State specific problems specially in the low
performing States continue to persist. Shortage of Health Workers, lack of awareness and
laxity in monitoring and supervision of the programme are some of the problems being
noticed in such States. Reported coverage of different vaccines under the Routine
Immunization Programme confirms the Committee’s apprehensions that in some of the
States like Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Manipur, position is very unsatisfactory.
The Committee would like to point out that the steps taken for strengthening the Routine
Immunization Programme like recruitment of health workers, regular reviews at all levels
and catch up rounds in poor performing States do not seem to have yielded the desired
results. The Committee can only say that catch-up rounds in poor performance States with
the districts identified before hand is the most important step for effective reduction in the
number of un-immunized and partially immunized children. Entire focus of the
Implementing agencies should be on this alone. (Para 9.15)
The Committee understands that the three pioneer Institutes namely Central
Research Institute (CRI), Kasauli in Himachal Pradesh, Pasteur Institute of India (PTI),
Koonoor, Tamil Nadu and the BCG Vaccine Laboratory (BCGVL) in Chennai, Tamil Nadu

I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and
Family Welfare, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do
hereby present this Twenty-ninth Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand
No.48) of the Department of Health Research, Ministry of  Health and Family Welfare for the year
2008-09.
2. The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from
the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and also heard the
Secretary and other officials of that Department on the said Demands for Grants in its meeting held
on 8th April, 2008.
3. The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meeting held on
the 25th April, 2008.
AMAR SINGH
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
25th April,  2008 Department-related Parliamentary
Vaisakha 5, 1930 (Saka) Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare.

1
REPORT
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH RESEARCH
I. INTRODUCTION
1.1 The Department of Health Research has been created in the Ministry by amending Allocation
of Business Rules. The President of India had notified creation of the Department of Health
Research under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on 17.09.2007.
1.2 The allocation of work to the newly created Department of Health Research is as under:—
• Promotion and co-ordination of basic, applied and clinical research including clinical
trials and operational research in areas related to medical, health biomedical and medical
profession and education through development of infrastructure, manpower and skills in
cutting edge areas and management of related information thereto;
• Promote and provide guidance of research governance issues, including ethical issues in
medical and health research;
• Inter-sectoral coordination and promotion of public private partnership in medical,
biomedical and health research related areas;
• Advanced training in research areas concerning medicine and health, including grant of
fellowships for such training in India and abroad; International co-operation in medical
and health research, including work related to international conferences in related areas
in India and abroad;
• Technical support for dealing with epidemics and natural calamities;
• Investigation of outbreaks due to new and exodic agents and
• development of tools for prevention;
• Matters relating to scientific societies and associations, charitable and religious
endowments in medicine and health research areas;
• Coordination between organizations and institutes under the Central and State
Governments in areas related to the subjects entrusted to the Department and for
promotion of special studies in medicine and health; and
• Indian Council of Medical Research.
1.3 The Secretary, in his presentation apprised the Committee that the Department is at the
inception stage, and will become fully operational after selection of an incumbent to the post of
a Secretary-cum-DG, ICMR. The Search Committee has been constituted under the Chairmanship
of the Cabinet Secretary for selecting a Director General of ICMR who would also be the
Secretary, Health Research.
1.4 The Committee feels that appointment of a full-fledged Director General, ICMR-
cum-Secretary, Department of Health Research is very important, for the Department,
being the nodal agency for promotion of Health Research, should be headed by a scientist
of repute and perpetuation of bureaucratic hold over the Department would defeat the very
purpose for which the Department of Health Research has been created. The Committee,
accordingly, urges upon the Department to finalise appointment of DG, ICMR-cum-
Secretary, Health Research at the earliest.

2
1.5 On a specific query about the appropriateness of medical education also being brought
under the purview of the Department of Health Research, the Committee has been given to
understand that Health Research and Medical Education have for long been two distinct areas on
account of functional and administrative reasons. The Committee is, however, not inclined to
agree with the contention of the Department. The Committee would like to point out that
both agricultural education and agricultural research have been placed under one
Department i.e. the Department of Agricultural Research and Education in the Ministry of
Agriculture. On the same analogy there should not be any difficulty in placing both medical
education and health research under the same Department. The Committee strongly feels
that this arrangement would be necessary for the sake of better coordination between the
different agencies involved in research work and medical educational institutions not only
providing clinical material for research but also engaged directly/indirectly in such projects.
Duplication of work undertaken by the different institutions/agencies in the field of medical
education and health research can also be made easily avoidable. The Committee is of the
view that medical education and health research cannot be placed in two distinct areas.
Instead both are complementary to each other in many ways. The Committee also feels that
with the merger of two separate Departments of Health and Family Welfare, the jurisdiction
of the Department has been expanded manifold. Besides, many Central Government
Hospitals, Premier Medical educational institutions and autonomous bodies, a very large
number of Central and centrally sponsored schemes are being administered/supervised by
the Department of Health and Family Welfare.
1.6 The Committee has been observing that with the setting up of more and more medical/
para-medical colleges in the country, vital area of medical education was not being taken care of
properly. It is a well-known fact that there is acute shortage of health care manpower of every
category in the country. The Committee is of the view that both for better management and proper
focus, subject of medical education needs to be brought together with health research. After being
part of the main Department for decades, Health Research has been assigned a distinct role with
the overall mandate of assigning health research its rightful place. The Committee feels that no
negative development would be there, if the subject of medical education also becomes part of the
Department of Health Research.
1.7 The Committee, therefore, recommends that both the medical education and Health
Research should be kept under one Department i.e. the Department of Health Education
and Research on the lines of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education for
better coordination and also for avoiding duplication of work amongst various institutions/
agencies engaged in Medical Education and Research.
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1 Total budgetary allocation made in BE 2008-09 in respect of the Department of
Health Research is Rs.531.75 crore; Rs.420 crore have been sanctioned on the plan side and
Rs.111.75 crore is the non-plan component against the projected demand of the Department for
Rs.1613.00 crores on the plan side and Rs.111.75 crores on the non-plan side.
2.2 On being asked whether the reduced allocation on the plan side would hamper
research projects of ICMR, the Financial Adviser (FA), ICMR, while deposing before the
Committee, clarified that the Eleventh Plan projections made by the ICMR was to the tune of
Rs.5000.00 crores against which Rs.4496.00 crores have been approved, which was well within
the range that had been projected. When asked to comment on the projected demand of the
Department for Rs.1613.00 crore for 2008-09, it was informed that the Department of Health
Research had made projections of Rs.1613.00 crore for 2008-09 because the Department wanted

3
to do major infrastructure upgradation and also start new activities in one go for which
Rs.600.00 crores had been projected and now that only Rs. 420.00 crores have been allocated for
2008-09, the Department would reschedule its activities and reorient the outflow of funds for the
remaining four years of the Eleventh Plan.
2.3 The Committee is not convinced with the clarification given by the representatives
of the Department. The Committee is unable to understand that in which manner the
Department will manage the expenditure on various activities out of meager allocation of
Rs.420 crores against the projected demand of Rs.1613 crores. The Committee has all
reasons to apprehend that the proposed major infrastructure upgradation as well as the new
activities proposed to be started by the Department are going to be affected badly. The
Committee desires that constraints of funds should not come in the way of the
infrastructure upgradation as well as the proposed new activities. The Committee, therefore,

III. INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH (ICMR)
3.1 The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), the apex body for the planning,
organization, implementation and coordination of the medical research in the country promotes
biomedical research through a network of its 21 permanent Institutes and 6 Regional Medical
Research Centres located throughout the country and also through grants-in-aid given to the
projects undertaken by the non-ICMR institutes.
3.2 ICMR promotes biomedical research in the country through intramural and extramural
research. During the year under report, the Council’s continued research and development on
critical areas of research such as management of communicable diseases, fertility control, maternal
and child health, nutritional deficiencies and disorders, solving environmental and occupational
health problems, research on non-communicable diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases,
haematological disorders, mental health, geriatric problems and research on traditional medicine.
3.3 The Committee notes that management of communicable diseases, fertility control,
maternal and child health care, nutritional deficiencies and disorders, environmental and
occupational health problems, non-communicable diseases like cancer, AIDS etc. have been
a serious cause of concern in the health sector. Some of the above problems have posed a
serious threat to a larger section of population of the country. This is the right time that
the ICMR should gear itself for a greater role in undertaking and coordinating the health
research undertaken by the different institutes/agencies as also it should take all out
efforts for minimizing the casualties as a result of the diseases referred to above
particularly due to the non-communicable diseases, nutritional deficiencies, maternal and
child mortality etc. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the ICMR should not leave
any stone unturned in the matter of management and control of the above diseases.

OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
I. INTRODUCTION
The Committee feels that appointment of a full-fledged Director General, ICMR-
cum-Secretary, Department of Health Research is very important, for, the Department,
being the nodal agency for promotion of Health Research, should be headed by a scientist
of repute and perpetuation of bureaucratic hold over the Department would defeat the very
purpose for which the Department of Health Research has been created. The Committee,
accordingly, urges upon the Department to finalise appointment of DG, ICMR-cum-
Secretary, Health Research at the earliest. (Para 1.4)
The Committee is, however, not inclined to agree with the contention of the
Department. The Committee would like to point out that both agricultural education and
agricultural research have been placed under one Department i.e.  the Department of
Agricultural Research and Education in the Ministry of Agriculture. On the same analogy
there should not be any difficulty in placing both medical education and health research
under the same Department. The Committee strongly feels that this arrangement would be
necessary for the sake of better coordination between the different agencies involved in
research work and medical educational institutions not only providing clinical material for
research but also engaged directly/indirectly in such projects. Duplication of work
undertaken by the different institutions/agencies in the field of medical education and
health research can also be made easily avoidable. The Committee is of the view that
medical education and health research cannot be placed in two distinct areas. Instead both
are complementary to each other in many ways. The Committee also feels that with the
merger of two separate Departments of Health and Family Welfare, the jurisdiction of the
Department has been expanded manifold. Besides, many Central Government Hospitals,
Premier Medical educational institutions and autonomous bodies, a very large number of
Central and Centrally sponsored schemes are being administered/supervised by the
Department of Health and Family Welfare. (Para 1.5)
The Committee, therefore, recommends that both the medical education and Health
Research should be kept under one Department i.e. the Department of Health Education
and Research on the lines of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education for
better coordination and also for avoiding duplication of work amongst various institutions/
agencies engaged in Medical Education and Research. (Para 1.7)

on Health and Family Welfare
           
REPORT
 
I.         INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Department of Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy which was set up by the Government of India
as an independent department in March, 1995, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was renamed as
Department of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH) in November, 2003.   The
main objective of the Department is to provide focused attention for the proper development and propagation of
Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, Homoeopathy, Yoga and Naturopathy and to fully utilize the potentials of these systems.
 
1.2       Thrust areas of the Department are: -
i)
                    Improvement and up-gradation of standards of education in AYUSH;
ii)                   Quality Control and Standardization of drugs;
iii)                 Ensuring sustained availability of raw materials, i.e. medicinal plants, metals, minerals and materials of
animal origin etc;
iv)                 Research & Development on the efficacy of the systems;
v)                  Participation of AYUSH in the National Health Care Delivery System & National Health & Family Welfare
Programme;
vi)                 Information, Education and Communication.
 
1.3       Over the years, there has been a steady growth in infrastructure.   At present, number of practitioners of AYUSH
in the country is 6,95,024.   There are 443 teaching institutions which include 4 Post-Graduate colleges imparting only
Postgraduate education.   Number of drug manufacturing units in the country is 9,257 and there are 3100 Hospitals.
II.            BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1       The Plan allocation for the Department in BE 2004-05 is Rs. 181.00 crores.   The Committee notes that Plan
allocation of Rs. 150.00 crores in BE 2003-04 was reduced to Rs. 135.00 crores at the RE stage due to the cuts imposed
by the Ministry of Finance.   The Committee was informed that funds amounting to Rs. 133.95 crores were utilized
during 2003-04 due to an overwhelming response received under some of the Centrally Sponsored Schemes like
Development of Institutions, Hospitals and Dispensaries etc.
2.2       The Committee was given to understand that higher allocation has been provided to the Department for 2004-05
in view of   almost all Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department having taken off well as also additional funds
required for the on-going research projects, strengthening the infrastructure of various autonomous bodies under the
Department.   The Committee is, however, not inclined to fully accept Department’s contention that almost all Centrally
Sponsored Schemes have taken off well in 2003-04.   The Committee would like to emphasise that it has taken years to
get started these Schemes.  Following Schemes were started during the Ninth Plan, some of them in the second year of
the Plan period, token funds continue to be allocated therefor: -
i)
                    ISM Polyclinic with regimental therapy, Panchkarma, Yoga and Naturopathy
ii)                   Opening of Speciality Clinics of ISMH in Govt. Hospitals
iii)                 Ayurvedic Park/Panchkarma in hotels.
 

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare
file:///D/health_family/3rdreport.htm[29-06-2016 14:37:52]
2.3       The Committee is constrained to note that allocation for the first two years of Tenth Plan for these Schemes
remains unutilized due to prolonged procedure of approval/appraisal. What is more disturbing is that the Scheme,
Ayurveda Park/Panchkarma in Hotels could not take off in 2003-04 for want of approval by SFC.   A provision of Rs. 1
crore for this Scheme was made in 2000-01, which continues to be provided with variations since then.   The Committee
apprehends that this Scheme will continue to be in a formulative stage during the Tenth Plan also with a token provision
of Rs. 1 lakh being made in 2004-05, the third year of Tenth Plan.
2.4       The Committee also observes that a number of Schemes under the Drug Quality Control have been started in
2002-03 with some allocation of funds which could not be utilized as the Schemes were in the formulation stage.  
Position was the same in 2003-04.    The Committee apprehends that there is no likelihood of any
improvement during 2004-05 also in view of the token provision being made for these Schemes for this year. The
Committee is of the view that Drug Quality Control is very vital for Indian Systems of Medicine  specially in view of 
maintaining their credibility both in the country and abroad.   The Committee would like to emphasise that prior to
launching a new scheme and keeping a provision therefor, all required procedural aspects should be taken care of.   The
Committee feels that necessary steps need to be taken for streamlining this procedure.
 
2.5       The Committee observes that against an initial Plan allocation of RS. 266.35 crores during the Ninth Plan,
subsequently raised to Rs. 364.43 crores, utilisation of funds was only Rs. 293.71 crores.   Plan allocation for the Tenth
Plan stands at Rs. 775.00 crores, more than double the allocation for Ninth Plan.   The Committee, however, notes that
during the first two years of Tenth Plan, utilisation can not be said to be satisfactory.    Against an allocation of Rs.
145.00 crores in BE 2003-04, reduced to Rs. 105.00 crores at RE stage, expenditure was Rs. 89.78 crores.   But, during
2003-04, the BE allocation of Rs. 145.00 crores, reduced to  Rs. 135.00 crores at RE stage, could be utilized. This year
2004-05 being the third year of the Tenth Plan, the Committee is of the view that this is the right time for an
appraisal/review of both existing and new schemes and taking necessary measures so as to have optimum and judicious
utilisation of allocated funds during the Tenth Plan.
 
IIICENTRAL PHARMACY COUNCIL FOR INDIAN MEDICINE AND HOMOEOPATHY
3.1       The Committee observes that the Department proposes to set up a Central Pharmacy Council for Indian
Medicine and Homoeopathy, a statutory body.  As per the Action Plan for 2004-05, the proposed Bill after getting
Cabinet approval is to be passed by both the Houses of Parliament and in the third quarter of the year, the Act is to be
enacted.   The Bill is yet to be passed by Parliament and the Committee finds only an Ad Hoc Council is proposed to be
set up in the last quarter of 2004-05.  The Committee is constrained to point out that the action for setting up a
Pharmacy Council started in mid-
Ninth Plan i.e. 2000-01 with token provision of Rs. 10.00 lakh each for setting up two separate  Councils – Indian
Homoeopathy Pharmacy Council and ISM  Pharmacy Council.  Subsequently, it seems that a decision was  taken to
have only one Council – Central Pharmacy Council  of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy in 2003-04 with a provision
of Rs. 19 lakhs therefor.   An allocation of Rs. 1.00 crore has been proposed for this purpose in Tenth Plan.   2004-05 is
the third year of Tenth Plan and not even a token allocation has been made in this year.  
 
3.2       The Committee expresses its serious concern over the progress made on such a vital issue and recommends that
the Department should make concerted efforts for getting the Bill passed during the Winter Session and  enacted during
2004-05 only and make a necessary allocation therefor at the RE stage. 

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare
file:///D/health_family/3rdreport.htm[29-06-2016 14:37:52]
 
(IV)            RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
4.1       The four Research Councils, viz. (i) Central Council for Research in Ayurveda and Siddha (CCRAS); (ii)
Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), (iii) Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy
(CCRH) and (iv) Central Council for Research in Yoga & Naturopathy (CCRYN) are the apex bodies for research in the
concerned systems of medicine.
 
4.2       The Committee notes that all the Research Councils are continuing to initiate and guide, develop and co-ordinate
scientific research in different aspects of respective systems, both fundamental and allied.   The Committee is happy to
observe that all these Councils have achieved the Physical targets of different research Programmes and allied matters,
in some cases exceeding the assigned targets.   The Committee, however, finds a disturbing trend.   A combined
building complex for all the Research Councils which were set up in 1978, was established in 1995.    Against an
allocation of Rs. 7.10 crores in Ninth Plan,  expenditure was only Rs. 4.16 crores.   During the first year of Tenth Plan
i.e. 2002-03, against an allocation of Rs. 1.10 crore, there was a saving of Rs. 13.20 lakhs, due to  the pending court 
decision of property tax issue.   The Committee is surprised to note
that during 2003-04, allocated funds of Rs. 1.20 crore could not be utilized for no evident justification.   The Committee
is apprehensive about the fate of funds (Rs. 1.50 crores) allocated for 2004-05.  The Committee strongly feels that the
Research Councils carrying out works having a far-reaching impact need to be housed in a well-maintained building.  
The Committee emphasizes that the Department should make concerted efforts to get resolved all the pending issues so
that funds meant for the maintenance of the building for Research Councils being judiciously utilized. 
 
(V)            AYURVEDA HOSPITAL, LODHI ROAD, NEW DELHI
5.1       The Committee notes that on its recommendations, the administrative control of the CGHS Ayurveda Hospital,
Lodhi Road, New Delhi was transferred to the Department of AYUSH in August, 2002 to streamline its functioning. 
However, the budget allocation of Rs. 50.00 lakhs for this Hospital could be made only in 2003-04.   Eeven that
allocation had to be drastically reduced to RS. 10.00 lakhs at the RE stage as the possession of building from civic
authorities was delayed.
 
5.2       The Committee, in the absence of any further explanation as to why the possession of building was delayed,
safely surmises that procedural formalities may be the main culprit behind the delayed possession of the building.
  Since the plan allocation for BE 2004-05 has been restored at Rs. 50 lakhs, the Committee hopes that the proposed
allocation will be fully utilized.
5.3       The Committee notes that in the absence of a regular Medical Superintendent, one of the Advisors of the
Department has been officiating as MS in addition to his normal duties.   What is more disturbing is that against the
sanctioned strength of 64 posts for the Hospital, only 32 posts are in position.   Details of Action Plan proposed by the
Department for this Hospital for 2004-05 clearly indicate that this year would not be sufficient to have the required staff
for   the Hospital.   The Committee enjoins upon the Department to take all the required measures without any delay for
making the Hospital fully functional.   The Department must not forget that the Hospital was transferred under its
administrative control for improving its functioning.
 
(VI)            SURVEY ON USAGE AND ACCEPTABILITY OF AYUSH (ISMH)

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare

            The objective of this Scheme is to collect the information on availability of facilities in the CGHS dispensaries
under AYUSH and level of utilisation/non-utilisation of   AYUSH services by the CGHS beneficiaries and also survey
of selected teaching hospitals under AYUSH for collecting information on available facilities and perception of
indoor/outdoor patients.  The Committee notes that this survey continued during Ninth Plan but not on a regular basis.  
What is more surprising is that during 2002-03, the first year of Tenth Plan, out of an allocation of Rs. 60 lakhs, only
Rs. 7.60 lakhs could be spent, the reason being non-approval of first survey, second survey being approved for Rs.7.60
lakhs.   During 2003-04, situation deteriorated as only Rs. 5.70 lakhs could be utilized against a meagre allocation of Rs.
12.00 lakhs due to delay in the finalisation of the survey instruments and consequently survey programme being
delayed.  Allocation of only Rs. 6.00 lakhs in 2004-05 clearly indicates the level of importance being given to this
survey programme.   The Committee is of the view that surveys are meant to be completed in a time-bound manner
otherwise the very purpose of undertaking them gets defeated.   The Committee therefore recommends that this survey
should be expedited so that assessment results could be put to use for expansion of AYUSH system of medicine.
 
(VII)             EXPANSION OF AYUSH DISPENSARIES IN CGHS.
7.1            Expansion of AYUSH (ISMH) Dispensaries in CGHS was another new Scheme proposed during Ninth
Plan.   The Scheme remained conceptual as only a  token allocation of Rs. 6.00 lakhs was made which could not be
utilized.   Position was the same in 2002-03 with the provision of Rs. 50 lakhs remaining unutilized.  The Committee  is
surprised to note that out of  an allocation of Rs. 86.00 lakhs for 2003-04 and  in spite of Director, CGHS being
authorized to utilize this amount out of the Budget head of Department of AYUSH for opening of 2 Ayurveda, 2
Homoeopathic, one Unani and one Siddha dispensaries and one Yoga Centre in  the premises of existing Allopathic
CGHS dispensaries only the location could be identified for opening of these dispensaries,  
Ayurveda & Homoeopathic at Trivandrum and Guwahati and Unani, Siddha & Yoga at Delhi.   The Committee is
constrained to note that whereas dispensaries at Trivandrum and Delhi are expected to start functioning, more time is
required for starting the Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic dispensaries at Guwahati.  
 
7.2       The Committee is not prepared to accept that non-availability of manpower was the reason for the allocation
remaining unspent.   The Committee finds it hard to believe that in a country like India, so well endowed in terms of its
human resources, the Department could not find suitable manpower, resulting in delayed  opening of dispensaries.  The
Committee is not satisfied with the temporary measures undertaken by the Department by  transferring senior level
Medical Officers  of concerned system and posting them to each of the locations and also hiring  the services of a
second doctor  and the Pharmacist in each of these dispensaries.    As the Plan allocation for BE 2004-05 has been
substantially increased to Rs. 1 crore 30 lakhs, the Committee recommends that the Department should take necessary
steps so that the proposed expansion/opening of AYUSH dispensaries in CGHS can actually take place during the
current financial year.  
 
(VIII) NATIONAL  AYURVEDIC HOSPITAL IN DELHI
8.1       Setting up of a National Ayurvedic Hospital in Delhi was one of the new Schemes proposed  in Ninth Plan for
which a nominal provision of Rs. 5.00 lakhs was made in 2000-01  which could not be utilized.   However, during 2001-
02, the last year of Ninth Plan against an allocation of Rs. 1 lakh only, expenditure incurred was Rs. 2.18 lakhs.  During
the Tenth Plan, against an allocation of RS. 2.00 crores and Rs.1.00 crores in 2002-03 and 2003-04, expenditure
incurred is only Rs. 12.60 lakhs and Rs. 15.00 lakhs respectively.   The Committee is surprised to note that it has taken

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare

four years to purchase the required land and getting in-principle approval of Ministry of Finance for setting up the
Hospital in Govt. sector which could be received on 3 rd October, 2003.   The Committee  apprehends that this Hospital
will perhaps remain on paper during Tenth Plan also.     Out of Rs. 15.00 crores earmarked for this Project in 
 
Tenth Plan, allocation  of only Rs. 1.00 crore has been  proposed  for 2004-05.  Activities planned for 2004-05 in Action
Plan confirm Committee’s apprehension.  As indicated by the Department, they have to seek additional land from DDA
in accordance with  CCIM norms of 10 acre land area of establishment  of new UG/PG Ayurved College/Institute.  
EFC approval would be dependent upon release of land by DDA.  
 
8.2       The Committee is constrained to note that only noteworthy achievement in this ambitious Project is the change
in the name from National Ayurvedic Hospital to All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi.    The Committee
apprehends that by the time all the necessary formalities are completed, initial cost of the Project would become
meaningless.   The Committee would like to emphasise that the Department should take all the required steps to
expedite this Project.  
 
(IX) NATIONAL MEDICINAL PLANTS BOARD
9.1       The National Medicinal Plants Board was established in the year 2000 with the  primary objectives of
establishing an agency which would be responsible for co-ordination of all matters relating to medicinal plants,
including  drawing up policies and strategies for conservation, proper harvesting, cost-effective cultivation, marketing of
raw material in order to protect, sustain and develop this sector.
 
9.2       The Committee notes that 31 State Medicinal Plants Boards have been set up in 26 States and 5 UTs.   So far 32
medicinal plants which are in great demand both  in domestic and international markets have been identified at national
level for cultivation, conservation and development. The Committee was informed that during the last three years, the
Board has sanctioned 1066 projects worth Rs. 41.34 crore covering 25,500 acres of land under cultivation and 28,500
acres of land under conservation.
 
9.3       The Committee observes that the Department is  also implementing a Central Scheme for Development and
Cultivation of Medicinal Plants whereunder  financial assistance is provided for Govt./Semi-Govt
organizations/autonomous/statutory bodies/scientific institutions including the agriculture/horticulture Universities for
setting
up of medicinal plant gardens and developing Agri-techniques of  medicinal plants.   The Committee finds that during
2003-04, out of an allocation of  Rs. 1.00 crore, funds amounting Rs. 95.65 lakhs could not be utilized.   The
Committee   was given to understand that  the scheme was put on hold for review and restructuring as it was not giving
expected results.   During the Ninth Plan, out of allocation of Rs. 8.40 crores, only Rs. 6.96 crores – could be utilized.  
The Committee strongly feels that with the setting up of a Medicinal Plant Board, there is no need for running a separate
Scheme and the existing Scheme should be administered by the Board after making the required changes.   The
Secretary gave the impression during the course  of deliberation  with the Committee   that such a decision had already
been taken by the Department.   The Committee however, is surprised to note that a provision of RS. 50 lakhs has been
proposed for 2004-05 and a proper Action Plan has been also drawn for administering that Scheme.   The Committee is
of the view that the Department should take a proper decision on this issue without any further delay.
 

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare

9.4       The Committee is in agreement with the Department’s view that it is necessary to strengthen the Board with
appropriate infrastructure and logistic support.  The Committee is aware that additional allocation for professional
achievements and captive cultivation of medicinal plants will be required.   The Committee would like to point out that
the idea of having a Board of Medicinal Plants  come into  place with a token grant of Rs. 1.00 lakh in  1999-2000, the
mid-year of Ninth Plan, and 2004-05 is the mid-term of the next Plan and still the Board lacks proper infrastructure. 
The Committee feels that the Department should give priority improving the infrastructure of the Board.
 
(X)            STRENGTHENING OF PHARMACOPOEIAL LABORATORIES
10.1     PLIM and HPL at Ghaziabad are the two Laboratories running for a number of years.  One of the main tasks
assigned to these Laboratories is to maintain quality control of such drugs.  The Committee, however, finds the
expenditure phase very discouraging.   During the Ninth Plan, against an allocation of Rs. 7.20 crores, expenditure
figures stand
at Rs.  2.72 crones only.   During 2002-03, there was under-utilisation of funds at PLIM due to non-creating of posts.  
Position did not improve in the second year and the reasons may be the same – non-creation of posts.  
 
10.2     The Committee is perturbed to note that even after such a considerable time, proper infrastructure is still not
there.  The Committee strongly feels that required action   has to be taken at the earliest for creating and filling up of
posts.
XI            QUALITY CONTROL
11.1            Committee’s attention has been drawn by a number of Fake herbal products and Ayurvedic products and
medicines claiming cure of a number of diseases readily available in the country.   On a specific query about the
preventive action taken by the Department  in this regard, the Committee was informed that the Drugs & Cosmetics Act,
1940 and Rules  thereunder regulate the quality standards of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani & Homoeopathy drugs. 
Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani medicines are manufactured under a valid Drug Manufacturing license  which is renewed
every three years.  Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) under Schedule T of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act which  call
for hygienic conditions, proper manufacturing processes and quality assurance of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani drugs  
have become mandatory with effect from June 2002.
 
11.2     The Committee was informed that pharmacopoeial standards of 324 Ayurvedic and 45 Unani drugs have been
published by Government of India and it is obligatory for the manufacturers to comply with these standards.
 
11.3     The Committee notes that licensing and registration of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani drugs is done by the State
Licensing Authorities.  Govt. of India provides maximum of Rs. 1 crore each to State Drug Testing Labs as well as State
Pharmacies of ISMH for the component of renovation of building procurement of   modern equipments and assistance
for human resource for State Drug Testing Labs on contractual basis.  The Committee was informed that 21 State Drugs
Testing Labs and 37 State Pharmacies have been assisted so far and an amount of RS. 45.62 crore has been released so
far as grants-in-aid.
11.4     The Committee   observes that following other schemes are listed under Drugs Quality Control: -
i)
                  Use of modern technology and biotechnology;
ii)                Scheme for Acquisition of ISO Quality Control Certification for ISMH industry;
iii)               Scheme for introduction for ASU mark for quality certification.

iv)              Regulation of health food supplements;
v)                Support to ISMH industry for creation of labs/quality control facilities;
vi)              Strengthening of enforcement mechanism for quality control; and
vii)             Assistance to units obtaining GMP certification.
 
11.5     The Committee notes that for all these schemes indicated above, BE allocation, token or otherwise during 2002-
03 was either reduced or totally withdrawn.   Position was the same during 2003-04.    Schemes simply continue to exist
on paper.   The Committee apprehends that during 2004-05 also, the Department does not anticipate their taking off   as
provision has been made in respect of only the following schemes: -
 i)              Use of    technology - Bio-technology                       -  Rs. 100 lakhs
ii)         Support of ISMH industry for creation of Labs/Quality                   - Rs. 150 lakhs control – facilities.
 
iii)          Strengthening of enforcement mechanism for      -  Rs. 50 lakhs
  quality control
iv)              Assistance for units obtaining GMP certification             - Rs.100 lakhs
 
The Committee emphasizes that schemes should be launched only when all the exercise/requisite formalities have been
completed and also after exploring the   feasibility of the scheme thereof.   The Committee hopes that the Department
will make concerted efforts   to start these schemes during the current year itself.
 
11.6
          The Committee was given to understand that there is no separate body constituted
exclusively to provide accreditation to medicinal claims.   Any claim received for Ayurvedic and Siddha medicine is
forwarded to the Central Council for Research of Ayurveda and Siddha for verification which has developed a format to
verify such claims.   If the Council finds substance in the claim, the documents supplied by the claimant are analysed
and the claim put up to the Scientific Advisory Committee of the Council.  If required, clinical trial is conducted.
 
11.7     The Committee expresses its serious concern about the variety of drugs of ISMH, particularly Ayurveda easily
available in the country.   It seems that manufacturers of such drugs and also doctors prescribing such drugs have
nothing to fear.   The Committee would like to mention that, in its 143
rd  Report presented to the House in December,
2003, the Committee had drawn the attention of the Department to advertisements by a doctor from Rishikesh claiming
to treat and cure epilepsy.  At that time too, the Department had justified their  action saying that the clinical data had
not been made available to  the Department for verification.  The Committee had then drawn the attention of the
Department to a specific Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question 3718 dt. 24.4.2000. As per the reply, to the Question, a team
of doctors was deputed by IMA to Rishikesh in 2000.  IMA found that Dr. R.K. Gupta was prescribing aurvedic
medicines, having no proven effect on  the patients of  epilepsy.  The Central Council of Ayurvedic Medicines took up
the matter with the Controller, Bhartiya Chikitsa Parishad, Lucknow.  The Committee was subsequently informed that
the State Government of Uttaranchal was asked to investigate the matter and take appropriate action under the Drugs      
Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act vide a letter dated 3
rd June, 2003.  Thereafter, a reminder was sent on
10th September, 2003.
 

3rd Report of COmmittee on Health And Family Welfare
file:///D/health_family/3rdreport.htm[29-06-2016 14:37:52]
11.8     The Committee expresses its serious concern on the pace of investigation in this particular case.  It is an example
of the lack of seriousness on the part of the Department towards such a sensitive issue which has a far-reaching impact. 
It has taken four and a half years to initiate legal action against a person who was playing with the lives of a very large
number of people by prescribing toxic and dangerous
 
drugs.  This could be possible only after the matter was highlighted through a Rajya Sabha Question which drew the
attention of the Committee on HRD.  The Committee believes that things would not have moved, had the matter not
been reported by it and pursued with the Department.  The Committee is of the view that the Department should take the
initiative in the event of such cases coming to its notice, by media or otherwise by taking up with the concerned State
Government and monitoring the outcome of the investigation if any initiated by the State authorities.                             
 
(XII) INDIAN MEDICINES PHARMACEUTICAL CORPORATION LIMITED (IMPCL) MOHAN (ALMORA),
UTTARANCHAL
12.1     Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation Ltd. is a Central Public Sector Undertaking  under the
administrative control of the Department having Registered Office & Factory at Mohan, Distt. Almora, Uttaranchal.
  The primary objective  of the Company is to  manufacture & supply authentic quality Ayurvedic & Unani medicines to
the CGHS and other Govt. Hospitals/dispensaries.   The company also sells its products to certain related Departments
of State Govts.  and other institutions and also in the open market.
12.2     The Committee was informed that a provision of Rs. 2.00 crore  was made in BE 2003-04 for investment in
IMPCL as it was expected that the first phase of modernization would be  completed and further funds were provided
for  taking up the second phase of modernization.   The Committee was given to understand that  implementation of the
first phase for  which an amount of Rs. 1.00 crore shared by the Central  and State Govt. of  Uttranchal  at  51.49 ratio
and given in March, 2001 got delayed due to sudden resignation of the then MD.   The situation was reviewed at RE
stage and it was found that IMPCL would not be in a position to utilize the funds meant for the second phase of
modernization during the year 2003-04.   Therefore, the allotted amount was reduced to a token amount of Rs. 1 lakh. 
The Department further informed that an amount of Rs. 0.51 crore has been kept for BE 2004-05 for IMPCL
accordingly.   As the first phase of modernization has been completed after joining of the new MD, it  has been planned
to take up the second phase of modernization during the current financial year. 
12.3     The Committee finds the explanation given by the Department for non-utilisation of funds meant for
expansion/strengthening of IMPCL, a public sector undertaking unreasonable.   The Committee is not inclined to
believe that the post of MD lying vacant can result in bringing the activities of a company to a standstill.    The
Committee finds it unprecedented and ridiculous that the expenditure of a Government of India undertaking is so much
dependent upon one official and that his absence has caused complete non-utilisation of funds by it.   This the
Committee feels is the worst that could happen to an institution of public importance and recommends that such
situation should not recur in future.

            The objective of this Scheme is to collect the information on availability of facilities in the CGHS dispensaries

of selected teaching hospitals under AYUSH for collecting information on available facilities and perception of
indoor/outdoor patients.  The Committee notes that this survey continued during Ninth Plan but not on a regular basis.  
What is more surprising is that during 2002-03, the first year of Tenth Plan, out of an allocation of Rs. 60 lakhs, only
